 16143	    def encode(self, text):
 16144	        """Return text with 'problematic' characters escaped.
 16145	
 16146	        * Escape the special printing characters ``# $ % & ~ _ ^ \\ { }``,
 16147	          square brackets ``[ ]``, double quotes and (in OT1) ``< | >``.
 16148	        * Translate non-supported Unicode characters.
 16149	        * Separate ``-`` (and more in literal text) to prevent input ligatures.
 16150	        """
 16151	        if self.verbatim:
 16152	            return text
 16153	        # Set up the translation table:
 16154	        table = CharMaps.alltt.copy()
 16155	        if not self.alltt:
 16156	            table.update(CharMaps.special)
 16157	        # keep the underscore in citation references
 16158	        if self.inside_citation_reference_label and not self.alltt:
 16159	            del table[ord('_')]
 16160	        # Workarounds for OT1 font-encoding
 16161	        if self.font_encoding in ['OT1', ''] and not self.is_xetex:
 16162	            # * out-of-order characters in cmtt
 16163	            if self.literal:
 16164	                # replace underscore by underlined blank,
 16165	                # because this has correct width.
 16166	                table[ord('_')] = '\\underline{~}'
 16167	                # the backslash doesn't work, so we use a mirrored slash.
 16168	                # \reflectbox is provided by graphicx:
 16169	                self.requirements['graphicx'] = self.graphicx_package
 16170	                table[ord('\\')] = '\\reflectbox{/}'
 16171	            # * ``< | >`` come out as different chars (except for cmtt):
 16172	            else:
 16173	                table[ord('|')] = '\\textbar{}'
 16174	                table[ord('<')] = '\\textless{}'
 16175	                table[ord('>')] = '\\textgreater{}'
 16176	        if self.insert_non_breaking_blanks:
 16177	            table[ord(' ')] = '~'
 16178	            # tab chars may occur in included files (literal or code)
 16179	            # quick-and-dirty replacement with spaces
 16180	            # (for better results use `--literal-block-env=lstlisting`)
 16181	            table[ord('\t')] = '~' * self.settings.tab_width
 16182	        # Unicode replacements for 8-bit tex engines (not required with XeTeX)
 16183	        if not self.is_xetex:
 16184	            if not self.latex_encoding.startswith('utf8'):
 16185	                table.update(CharMaps.unsupported_unicode)
 16186	                table.update(CharMaps.utf8_supported_unicode)
 16187	                table.update(CharMaps.textcomp)
 16188	            table.update(CharMaps.pifont)
 16189	            # Characters that require a feature/package to render
 16190	            for ch in text:
 16191	                cp = ord(ch)
 16192	                if cp in CharMaps.textcomp and not self.fallback_stylesheet:
 16193	                    self.requirements['textcomp'] = PreambleCmds.textcomp
 16194	                elif cp in CharMaps.pifont:
 16195	                    self.requirements['pifont'] = '\\usepackage{pifont}'
 16196	                # preamble-definitions for unsupported Unicode characters
 16197	                elif (self.latex_encoding == 'utf8'
 16198	                      and cp in CharMaps.unsupported_unicode):
 16199	                    self.requirements['_inputenc'+str(cp)] = (
 16200	                        '\\DeclareUnicodeCharacter{%04X}{%s}'
 16201	                        % (cp, CharMaps.unsupported_unicode[cp]))
 16202	        text = text.translate(table)
 16203	
 16204	        # Break up input ligatures e.g. '--' to '-{}-'.
 16205	        if not self.is_xetex:  # Not required with xetex/luatex
 16206	            separate_chars = '-'
 16207	            # In monospace-font, we also separate ',,', '``' and "''" and some
 16208	            # other characters which can't occur in non-literal text.
 16209	            if self.literal:
 16210	                separate_chars += ',`\'"<>'
 16211	            for char in separate_chars * 2:
 16212	                # Do it twice ("* 2") because otherwise we would replace
 16213	                # '---' by '-{}--'.
 16214	                text = text.replace(char + char, char + '{}' + char)
 16215	
 16216	        # Literal line breaks (in address or literal blocks):
 16217	        if self.insert_newline:
 16218	            lines = text.split('\n')
 16219	            # Add a protected space to blank lines (except the last)
 16220	            # to avoid ``! LaTeX Error: There's no line here to end.``
 16221	            for i, line in enumerate(lines[:-1]):
 16222	                if not line.lstrip():
 16223	                    lines[i] += '~'
 16224	            text = (r'\\' + '\n').join(lines)
 16225	        if self.literal and not self.insert_non_breaking_blanks:
 16226	            # preserve runs of spaces but allow wrapping
 16227	            text = text.replace('  ', ' ~')
 16228	        return text

 16253	    def ids_to_labels(self, node, set_anchor=True, protect=False,

 16327	    def term_postfix(self, node):
 16328	        """
 16329	        Return LaTeX code required between term or field name and content.
 16330	
 16331	        In a LaTeX "description" environment (used for definition
 16332	        lists and non-docinfo field lists), a ``\\leavevmode``
 16333	        between an item's label and content ensures the correct
 16334	        placement of certain block constructs.
 16335	        """
 16336	        for child in node:
 16337	            if not isinstance(child, (nodes.Invisible, nodes.footnote,
 16338	                                      nodes.citation)):
 16339	                break
 16340	        else:
 16341	            return ''
 16342	        if isinstance(child, (nodes.container, nodes.compound)):
 16343	            return self.term_postfix(child)
 16344	        if isinstance(child, nodes.image):
 16345	            return '\\leavevmode\n'  # Images get an additional newline.
 16346	        if not isinstance(child, (nodes.paragraph, nodes.math_block)):
 16347	            return '\\leavevmode'
 16348	        return ''

 16702	    def make_title(self):
 16703	        # Auxiliary function called by `self.depart_document()`.
 16704	        #
 16705	        # Append ``\title``, ``\author``, and ``\date`` to "titledata".
 16706	        # (We need all three, even if empty, to prevent errors
 16707	        # and/or automatic display of the current date by \maketitle.)
 16708	        # Append ``\maketitle`` to "body_pre_docinfo" parts.
 16709	        #
 16710	        # \title
 16711	        title_arg = [''.join(self.title)]  # ensure len == 1
 16712	        if self.title:
 16713	            title_arg += self.title_labels
 16714	        if self.subtitle:
 16715	            title_arg += [r'\\',
 16716	                          r'\DUdocumentsubtitle{%s}' % ''.join(self.subtitle),
 16717	                          ] + self.subtitle_labels
 16718	        self.titledata.append(r'\title{%s}' % '%\n  '.join(title_arg))
 16719	        # \author
 16720	        author_arg = ['\\\\\n'.join(author_entry)
 16721	                      for author_entry in self.author_stack]
 16722	        self.titledata.append(r'\author{%s}' %
 16723	                              ' \\and\n'.join(author_arg))
 16724	        # \date
 16725	        self.titledata.append(r'\date{%s}' % ', '.join(self.date))

 16763	    def insert_additional_table_colum_delimiters(self):
 16764	        while self.active_table.get_rowspan(

 16769	    def visit_entry(self, node):
 16770	        # cell separation
 16771	        if self.active_table.get_entry_number() == 0:
 16772	            self.insert_additional_table_colum_delimiters()
 16773	        else:
 16774	            self.out.append(' & ')
 16775	
 16776	        # multirow, multicolumn
 16777	        if 'morerows' in node and 'morecols' in node:
 16778	            raise NotImplementedError('Cells that span multiple rows *and* '
 16779	                                      'columns currently not supported '
 16780	                                      'by the LaTeX writer')
 16781	            # TODO: should be possible with LaTeX, see e.g.
 16782	            # http://texblog.org/2012/12/21/multi-column-and-multi-row-cells-in-latex-tables/
 16783	        # multirow in LaTeX simply will enlarge the cell over several rows
 16784	        # (the following n if n is positive, the former if negative).
 16785	        if 'morerows' in node:
 16786	            self.requirements['multirow'] = r'\usepackage{multirow}'
 16787	            mrows = node['morerows'] + 1
 16788	            self.active_table.set_rowspan(
 16789	                            self.active_table.get_entry_number(), mrows)
 16790	            self.out.append('\\multirow{%d}{%s}{' %
 16791	                            (mrows, self.active_table.get_column_width()))
 16792	            self.context.append('}')

 16794	            # the vertical bar before column is missing if it is the first
 16795	            # column. the one after always.
 16796	            if self.active_table.get_entry_number() == 0:
 16797	                bar1 = self.active_table.get_vertical_bar()
 16798	            else:
 16799	                bar1 = ''
 16800	            mcols = node['morecols'] + 1
 16801	            self.out.append('\\multicolumn{%d}{%s%s%s}{' %
 16802	                            (mcols,
 16803	                             bar1,
 16804	                             self.active_table.get_multicolumn_width(
 16805	                                 self.active_table.get_entry_number(), mcols),
 16806	                             self.active_table.get_vertical_bar()))
 16807	            self.context.append('}')
 16808	        else:
 16809	            self.context.append('')

 16812	        if len(node) and (isinstance(node.parent.parent, nodes.thead)
 16813	                          or self.active_table.is_stub_column()):
 16814	            self.out.append('\\textbf{')

 16816	        else:
 16817	            self.context.append('')

 16820	        if (not self.active_table.colwidths_auto
 16821	            and self.out[-1].endswith("{")
 16822	            and node.astext()):

 16839	    def visit_enumerated_list(self, node):
 16840	        # enumeration styles:
 16841	        types = {'': '',
 16842	                 'arabic': 'arabic',
 16843	                 'loweralpha': 'alph',
 16844	                 'upperalpha': 'Alph',
 16845	                 'lowerroman': 'roman',
 16846	                 'upperroman': 'Roman'}
 16847	        # default LaTeX enumeration labels:
 16848	        default_labels = [
 16849	                          # (präfix, enumtype, suffix)
 16850	                          ('',  'arabic', '.'),  # 1.
 16851	                          ('(', 'alph',   ')'),  # (a)
 16852	                          ('',  'roman',  '.'),  # i.
 16853	                          ('',  'Alph',   '.')]  # A.
 16854	
 16855	        prefix = ''
 16856	        if self.compound_enumerators:
 16857	            if (self.section_prefix_for_enumerators and self.section_level
 16858	                and not self._enumeration_counters):
 16859	                prefix = '.'.join(str(n) for n in
 16860	                                  self._section_number[:self.section_level]
 16861	                                  ) + self.section_enumerator_separator
 16862	            if self._enumeration_counters:
 16863	                prefix += self._enumeration_counters[-1]
 16864	        prefix += node.get('prefix', '')
 16865	        enumtype = types[node.get('enumtype', 'arabic')]
 16866	        suffix = node.get('suffix', '.')
 16867	
 16868	        enum_level = len(self._enumeration_counters)+1
 16869	        counter_name = 'enum' + roman.toRoman(enum_level).lower()
 16870	        label = r'%s\%s{%s}%s' % (prefix, enumtype, counter_name, suffix)
 16871	        self._enumeration_counters.append(label)
 16872	
 16873	        self.duclass_open(node)
 16874	        if enum_level <= 4:
 16875	            self.out.append('\\begin{enumerate}')
 16876	            if (prefix, enumtype, suffix) != default_labels[enum_level-1]:
 16877	                self.out.append('\n\\renewcommand{\\label%s}{%s}' %
 16878	                                (counter_name, label))
 16879	        else:
 16880	            self.fallbacks[counter_name] = '\\newcounter{%s}' % counter_name
 16881	            self.out.append('\\begin{list}')
 16882	            self.out.append('{%s}' % label)
 16883	            self.out.append('{\\usecounter{%s}}' % counter_name)
 16884	        if 'start' in node:
 16885	            self.out.append('\n\\setcounter{%s}{%d}' %
 16886	                            (counter_name, node['start']-1))

 17050	    def to_latex_length(self, length_str, pxunit=None):
 17051	        """Convert `length_str` with rst length to LaTeX length
 17052	        """
 17053	        if pxunit is not None:
 17054	            warnings.warn(
 17055	                'The optional argument `pxunit` '
 17056	                'of LaTeXTranslator.to_latex_length() is ignored '
 17057	                'and will be removed in Docutils 0.21 or later',
 17058	                DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)
 17059	        match = re.match(r'(\d*\.?\d*)\s*(\S*)', length_str)
 17060	        if not match:
 17061	            return length_str
 17062	        value, unit = match.groups()[:2]
 17063	        # no unit or "DTP" points (called 'bp' in TeX):
 17064	        if unit in ('', 'pt'):
 17065	            length_str = '%sbp' % value
 17066	        # percentage: relate to current line width
 17067	        elif unit == '%':
 17068	            length_str = '%.3f\\linewidth' % (float(value)/100.0)
 17069	        elif self.is_xetex and unit == 'px':
 17070	            # XeTeX does not know the length unit px.
 17071	            # Use \pdfpxdimen, the macro to set the value of 1 px in pdftex.
 17072	            # This way, configuring works the same for pdftex and xetex.
 17073	            if not self.fallback_stylesheet:
 17074	                self.fallbacks['_providelength'] = PreambleCmds.providelength
 17075	            self.fallbacks['px'] = '\n\\DUprovidelength{\\pdfpxdimen}{1bp}\n'
 17076	            length_str = r'%s\pdfpxdimen' % value
 17077	        return length_str

 17213	    # the others we must use \ttfamily and \raggedright.

 17215	    # We can distinguish between the two kinds by the number of
 17216	    # siblings that compose this node: if it is composed by a

 17231	                                   r'\lstset{xleftmargin=\leftmargin}',
 17232	                    'listing': r'\usepackage{moreverb}',
 17233	                    'Verbatim': r'\usepackage{fancyvrb}',
 17234	                    'verbatimtab': r'\usepackage{moreverb}'}
 17235	
 17236	        literal_env = self.literal_block_env

 17477	    def has_unbalanced_braces(self, string):
 17478	        """Test whether there are unmatched '{' or '}' characters."""
 17479	        level = 0
 17480	        for ch in string:
 17481	            if ch == '{':
 17482	                level += 1
 17483	            if ch == '}':

 17485	            if level < 0:
 17486	                return True
 17487	        return level != 0

 17489	    def visit_reference(self, node):
 17490	        # We need to escape #, \, and % if we use the URL in a command.

 17492	                         ord('%'): '\\%',
 17493	                         ord('\\'): '\\\\',
 17494	                         }
 17495	        # external reference (URL)
 17496	        if 'refuri' in node:
 17497	            href = str(node['refuri']).translate(special_chars)
 17498	            # problematic chars double caret and unbalanced braces:
 17499	            if href.find('^^') != -1 or self.has_unbalanced_braces(href):
 17500	                self.error(
 17501	                    'External link "%s" not supported by LaTeX.\n'
 17502	                    ' (Must not contain "^^" or unbalanced braces.)' % href)
 17503	            if node['refuri'] == node.astext():
 17504	                self.out.append(r'\url{%s}' % href)
 17505	                raise nodes.SkipNode
 17506	            self.out.append(r'\href{%s}{' % href)
 17507	            return
 17508	        # internal reference
 17509	        if 'refid' in node:
 17510	            href = node['refid']
 17511	        elif 'refname' in node:
 17512	            href = self.document.nameids[node['refname']]
 17513	        else:
 17514	            raise AssertionError('Unknown reference.')
 17515	        if not self.is_inline(node):
 17516	            self.out.append('\n')
 17517	        self.out.append('\\hyperref[%s]{' % href)
 17518	        if self._reference_label:
 17519	            self.out.append('\\%s{%s}}' %
 17520	                            (self._reference_label, href.replace('#', '')))
 17521	            raise nodes.SkipNode

 17842	    def visit_contents(self, node):
 17843	        """Write the table of contents.
 17844	
 17845	        Called from visit_topic() for "contents" topics.
 17846	        """
 17847	        # requirements/setup for local ToC with package "minitoc",
 17848	        if self.use_latex_toc and 'local' in node['classes']:
 17849	            section_name = self.d_class.section(self.section_level)
 17850	            # minitoc only supports "part" and toplevel sections
 17851	            minitoc_names = {'part': 'part',
 17852	                             'chapter': 'mini',
 17853	                             'section': 'sect'}
 17854	            if 'chapter' in self.d_class.sections:
 17855	                del minitoc_names['section']
 17856	            try:
 17857	                mtc_name = minitoc_names[section_name]
 17858	            except KeyError:
 17859	                self.warn('Skipping local ToC at "%s" level.\n'
 17860	                          '  Feature not supported with option "use-latex-toc"'
 17861	                          % section_name, base_node=node)
 17862	                raise nodes.SkipNode
 17863	
 17864	        # labels and PDF bookmark (sidebar entry)
 17865	        self.out.append('\n')  # start new paragraph
 17866	        if node['names']:  # don't add labels just for auto-ids
 17867	            self.out += self.ids_to_labels(node, newline=True)
 17868	        if (isinstance(node.next_node(), nodes.title)
 17869	            and 'local' not in node['classes']
 17870	            and self.settings.documentclass != 'memoir'):
 17871	            self.out.append('\\pdfbookmark[%d]{%s}{%s}\n' %
 17872	                            (self.section_level+1,
 17873	                             node.next_node().astext(),
 17874	                             node.get('ids', ['contents'])[0]))
 17875	
 17876	        # Docutils generated contents list (no page numbers)
 17877	        if not self.use_latex_toc:
 17878	            self.fallbacks['toc-list'] = PreambleCmds.toc_list
 17879	            self.duclass_open(node)
 17880	            return
 17881	
 17882	        # ToC by LaTeX
 17883	        depth = node.get('depth', 0)
 17884	        maxdepth = len(self.d_class.sections)
 17885	        if isinstance(node.next_node(), nodes.title):
 17886	            title = self.encode(node[0].astext())
 17887	        else:
 17888	            title = ''
 17889	        if 'local' in node['classes']:
 17890	            # use the "minitoc" package
 17891	            self.requirements['minitoc'] = PreambleCmds.minitoc
 17892	            self.requirements['minitoc-'+mtc_name] = r'\do%stoc'%mtc_name
 17893	            self.requirements['minitoc-%s-depth' % mtc_name] = (

 17899	                offset['part'] = -1
 17900	            if depth:

 17902	                                (mtc_name, depth + offset[mtc_name]))
 17903	            # title:
 17904	            self.out.append('\\mtcsettitle{%stoc}{%s}\n' % (mtc_name, title))

 17906	            self.out.append('\\%stoc\n' % mtc_name)

 17910	                                % self.d_class.latex_section_depth(depth))

 18090	    def __init__(self):

 18100	        """Append the separator for table head."""

 18103	    def append_cell(self, cell_lines):
 18104	        """cell_lines is an array of lines"""
 18105	        start = 0
 18106	        if len(cell_lines) > 0 and cell_lines[0] == '.sp\n':
 18107	            start = 1
 18108	        self._rows[-1].append(cell_lines[start:])
 18109	        if len(self._coldefs) < len(self._rows[-1]):
 18110	            self._coldefs.append('l')
 18111	
 18112	    def _minimize_cell(self, cell_lines):
 18113	        """Remove leading and trailing blank and ``.sp`` lines"""
 18114	        while cell_lines and cell_lines[0] in ('\n', '.sp\n'):
 18115	            del cell_lines[0]
 18116	        while cell_lines and cell_lines[-1] in ('\n', '.sp\n'):
 18117	            del cell_lines[-1]
 18118	
 18119	    def as_list(self):
 18120	        text = ['.TS\n']
 18121	        text.append(' '.join(self._options) + ';\n')
 18122	        text.append('|%s|.\n' % ('|'.join(self._coldefs)))
 18123	        for row in self._rows:
 18124	            # row = array of cells. cell = array of lines.
 18125	            text.append('_\n')       # line above
 18126	            text.append('T{\n')
 18127	            for i in range(len(row)):
 18128	                cell = row[i]
 18129	                self._minimize_cell(cell)
 18130	                text.extend(cell)
 18131	                if not text[-1].endswith('\n'):
 18132	                    text[-1] += '\n'
 18133	                if i < len(row)-1:
 18134	                    text.append('T}'+self._tab_char+'T{\n')
 18135	                else:
 18136	                    text.append('T}\n')
 18137	        text.append('_\n')
 18138	        text.append('.TE\n')
 18139	        return text

 21352	    def get_image_width_height(self, node, attr):
 21353	        size = None
 21354	        unit = None
 21355	        if attr in node.attributes:
 21356	            size = node.attributes[attr]
 21357	            size = size.strip()
 21358	            # For conversion factors, see:
 21359	            # http://www.unitconversion.org/unit_converter/typography-ex.html
 21360	            try:
 21361	                if size.endswith('%'):
 21362	                    if attr == 'height':
 21363	                        # Percentage allowed for width but not height.
 21364	                        raise ValueError('percentage not allowed for height')
 21365	                    size = size.rstrip(' %')
 21366	                    size = float(size) / 100.0
 21367	                    unit = '%'
 21368	                else:
 21369	                    size, unit = self.convert_to_cm(size)
 21370	            except ValueError as exp:
 21371	                self.document.reporter.warning(
 21372	                    'Invalid %s for image: "%s".  '
 21373	                    'Error: "%s".' % (
 21374	                        attr, node.attributes[attr], exp))

 21377	    def convert_to_cm(self, size):
 21378	        """Convert various units to centimeters.
 21379	
 21380	        Note that a call to this method should be wrapped in:
 21381	            try: except ValueError:
 21382	        """
 21383	        size = size.strip()
 21384	        if size.endswith('px'):
 21385	            size = float(size[:-2]) * 0.026     # convert px to cm
 21386	        elif size.endswith('in'):
 21387	            size = float(size[:-2]) * 2.54      # convert in to cm
 21388	        elif size.endswith('pt'):
 21389	            size = float(size[:-2]) * 0.035     # convert pt to cm
 21390	        elif size.endswith('pc'):
 21391	            size = float(size[:-2]) * 2.371     # convert pc to cm
 21392	        elif size.endswith('mm'):
 21393	            size = float(size[:-2]) * 0.1       # convert mm to cm
 21394	        elif size.endswith('cm'):
 21395	            size = float(size[:-2])
 21396	        else:
 21397	            raise ValueError('unknown unit type')
 21398	        unit = 'cm'
 21399	        return size, unit

 21419	    def get_image_scaled_width_height(self, node, source):
 21420	        """Return the image size in centimeters adjusted by image attrs."""
 21421	        scale = self.get_image_scale(node)
 21422	        width, width_unit = self.get_image_width_height(node, 'width')
 21423	        height, _ = self.get_image_width_height(node, 'height')
 21424	        dpi = (72, 72)
 21425	        if PIL is not None and source in self.image_dict:
 21426	            filename, destination = self.image_dict[source]
 21427	            with PIL.Image.open(filename, 'r') as img:
 21428	                img_size = img.size
 21429	                dpi = img.info.get('dpi', dpi)
 21430	            # dpi information can be (xdpi, ydpi) or xydpi
 21431	            try:
 21432	                iter(dpi)
 21433	            except TypeError:
 21434	                dpi = (dpi, dpi)
 21435	        else:
 21436	            img_size = None
 21437	        if width is None or height is None:
 21438	            if img_size is None:
 21439	                raise RuntimeError(
 21440	                    'image size not fully specified and PIL not installed')
 21441	            if width is None:
 21442	                width = img_size[0]
 21443	                width = float(width) * 0.026        # convert px to cm
 21444	            if height is None:
 21445	                height = img_size[1]
 21446	                height = float(height) * 0.026      # convert px to cm
 21447	            if width_unit == '%':
 21448	                factor = width
 21449	                image_width = img_size[0]
 21450	                image_width = float(image_width) * 0.026    # convert px to cm
 21451	                image_height = img_size[1]
 21452	                image_height = float(image_height) * 0.026  # convert px to cm
 21453	                line_width = self.get_page_width()
 21454	                width = factor * line_width
 21455	                factor = (factor * line_width) / image_width
 21456	                height = factor * image_height
 21457	        width *= scale
 21458	        height *= scale
 21459	        width = '%.2fcm' % width
 21460	        height = '%.2fcm' % height
 21461	        return width, height

 21463	    def get_page_width(self):
 21464	        """Return the document's page width in centimeters."""
 21465	        root = self.get_dom_stylesheet()
 21466	        nodes = root.iterfind(
 21467	            './/{urn:oasis:names:tc:opendocument:xmlns:style:1.0}'
 21468	            'page-layout/'
 21469	            '{urn:oasis:names:tc:opendocument:xmlns:style:1.0}'
 21470	            'page-layout-properties')
 21471	        width = None
 21472	        for node in nodes:
 21473	            page_width = node.get(
 21474	                '{urn:oasis:names:tc:opendocument:xmlns:xsl-fo-compatible:1.0}'
 21475	                'page-width')
 21476	            margin_left = node.get(
 21477	                '{urn:oasis:names:tc:opendocument:xmlns:xsl-fo-compatible:1.0}'
 21478	                'margin-left')
 21479	            margin_right = node.get(
 21480	                '{urn:oasis:names:tc:opendocument:xmlns:xsl-fo-compatible:1.0}'
 21481	                'margin-right')
 21482	            if (page_width is None
 21483	                or margin_left is None
 21484	                or margin_right is None):
 21485	                continue
 21486	            try:
 21487	                page_width, _ = self.convert_to_cm(page_width)
 21488	                margin_left, _ = self.convert_to_cm(margin_left)
 21489	                margin_right, _ = self.convert_to_cm(margin_right)
 21490	            except ValueError:
 21491	                self.document.reporter.warning(
 21492	                    'Stylesheet file contains invalid page width '

 21494	            width = page_width - margin_left - margin_right
 21495	        if width is None:
 21496	            # We can't find the width in styles, so we make a guess.
 21497	            # Use a width of 6 in = 15.24 cm.

 22632	
 22633	OpenType fonts with PostScript outlines embed a completely independent
 22634	font file in Adobe's *Compact Font Format*. So dealing with OpenType fonts
 22635	requires also dealing with CFF. This module allows you to read and write
 22636	fonts written in the CFF format.

 22638	In 2016, OpenType 1.8 introduced the `CFF2 <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/cff2>`_
 22639	format which, along with other changes, extended the CFF format to deal with

 22678	class CFFFontSet(object):
 22679	    """A CFF font "file" can contain more than one font, although this is
 22680	    extremely rare (and not allowed within OpenType fonts).
 22681	
 22682	    This class is the entry point for parsing a CFF table. To actually
 22683	    manipulate the data inside the CFF font, you will want to access the
 22684	    ``CFFFontSet``'s :class:`TopDict` object. To do this, a ``CFFFontSet``
 22685	    object can either be treated as a dictionary (with appropriate
 22686	    ``keys()`` and ``values()`` methods) mapping font names to :class:`TopDict`
 22687	    objects, or as a list.
 22688	
 22689	    .. code:: python
 22690	
 22691	            from fontTools import ttLib
 22692	            tt = ttLib.TTFont("Tests/cffLib/data/LinLibertine_RBI.otf")
 22693	            tt["CFF "].cff
 22694	            # <fontTools.cffLib.CFFFontSet object at 0x101e24c90>
 22695	            tt["CFF "].cff[0] # Here's your actual font data
 22696	            # <fontTools.cffLib.TopDict object at 0x1020f1fd0>
 22697

 22699	
 22700	    def decompile(self, file, otFont, isCFF2=None):
 22701	        """Parse a binary CFF file into an internal representation. ``file``
 22702	        should be a file handle object. ``otFont`` is the top-level
 22703	        :py:class:`fontTools.ttLib.ttFont.TTFont` object containing this CFF file.
 22704	
 22705	        If ``isCFF2`` is passed and set to ``True`` or ``False``, then the
 22706	        library makes an assertion that the CFF header is of the appropriate
 22707	        version.
 22708	        """
 22709	
 22710	        self.otFont = otFont
 22711	        sstruct.unpack(cffHeaderFormat, file.read(3), self)
 22712	        if isCFF2 is not None:
 22713	            # called from ttLib: assert 'major' as read from file matches the

 22770	    def compile(self, file, otFont, isCFF2=None):

 22773	        :py:class:`fontTools.ttLib.ttFont.TTFont` object containing this CFF file.
 22774

 22776	        library makes an assertion that the CFF header is of the appropriate
 22777	        version.
 22778	        """

 22780	        if isCFF2 is not None:
 22781	            # called from ttLib: assert 'major' value matches expected version
 22782	            expected_major = 2 if isCFF2 else 1
 22783	            if self.major != expected_major:
 22784	                raise ValueError(
 22785	                    "Invalid CFF 'major' version: expected %d, found %d"
 22786	                    % (expected_major, self.major)
 22787	                )
 22788	        else:
 22789	            # use current 'major' value to determine output format
 22790	            assert self.major in (1, 2), "Unknown CFF format"
 22791	            isCFF2 = self.major == 2

 22793	        if otFont.recalcBBoxes and not isCFF2:
 22794	            for topDict in self.topDictIndex:
 22795	                topDict.recalcFontBBox()

 22797	        if not isCFF2:

 22799	        else:

 22802	        topCompiler = self.topDictIndex.getCompiler(strings, self, isCFF2=isCFF2)

 22805	            writer.add(sstruct.pack(cffHeaderFormat, self))
 22806	            # Note: topDictSize will most likely change in CFFWriter.toFile().
 22807	            self.topDictSize = topCompiler.getDataLength()
 22808	            writer.add(struct.pack(">H", self.topDictSize))
 22809	        else:

 22811	            self.offSize = 4  # will most likely change in CFFWriter.toFile().
 22812	            writer.add(sstruct.pack(cffHeaderFormat, self))
 22813	            writer.add(struct.pack("B", self.offSize))
 22814	        if not isCFF2:

 22816	            for name in self.fontNames:
 22817	                fontNames.append(name)
 22818	            writer.add(fontNames.getCompiler(strings, self, isCFF2=isCFF2))

 22820	        if not isCFF2:

 22822	        writer.add(self.GlobalSubrs.getCompiler(strings, self, isCFF2=isCFF2))

 22824	        for topDict in self.topDictIndex:
 22825	            if not hasattr(topDict, "charset") or topDict.charset is None:
 22826	                charset = otFont.getGlyphOrder()
 22827	                topDict.charset = charset
 22828	        children = topCompiler.getChildren(strings)
 22829	        for child in children:

 22957	class CFFWriter(object):
 22958	    """Helper class for serializing CFF data to binary. Used by
 22959	    :meth:`CFFFontSet.compile`."""
 22960	
 22961	    def __init__(self, isCFF2):
 22962	        self.data = []
 22963	        self.isCFF2 = isCFF2
 22964	
 22965	    def add(self, table):
 22966	        self.data.append(table)
 22967	
 22968	    def toFile(self, file):
 22969	        lastPosList = None
 22970	        count = 1
 22971	        while True:
 22972	            log.log(DEBUG, "CFFWriter.toFile() iteration: %d", count)
 22973	            count = count + 1
 22974	            pos = 0
 22975	            posList = [pos]
 22976	            for item in self.data:
 22977	                if hasattr(item, "getDataLength"):
 22978	                    endPos = pos + item.getDataLength()
 22979	                    if isinstance(item, TopDictIndexCompiler) and item.isCFF2:
 22980	                        self.topDictSize = item.getDataLength()
 22981	                else:
 22982	                    endPos = pos + len(item)
 22983	                if hasattr(item, "setPos"):
 22984	                    item.setPos(pos, endPos)
 22985	                pos = endPos
 22986	                posList.append(pos)
 22987	            if posList == lastPosList:
 22988	                break
 22989	            lastPosList = posList
 22990	        log.log(DEBUG, "CFFWriter.toFile() writing to file.")
 22991	        begin = file.tell()
 22992	        if self.isCFF2:
 22993	            self.data[1] = struct.pack(">H", self.topDictSize)
 22994	        else:
 22995	            self.offSize = calcOffSize(lastPosList[-1])
 22996	            self.data[1] = struct.pack("B", self.offSize)
 22997	        posList = [0]
 22998	        for item in self.data:
 22999	            if hasattr(item, "toFile"):
 23000	                item.toFile(file)
 23001	            else:
 23002	                file.write(item)
 23003	            posList.append(file.tell() - begin)
 23004	        assert posList == lastPosList

 23007	def calcOffSize(largestOffset):
 23008	    if largestOffset < 0x100:
 23009	        offSize = 1
 23010	    elif largestOffset < 0x10000:
 23011	        offSize = 2
 23012	    elif largestOffset < 0x1000000:
 23013	        offSize = 3
 23014	    else:
 23015	        offSize = 4
 23016	    return offSize

 23019	class IndexCompiler(object):
 23020	    """Base class for writing CFF `INDEX data <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/cff2#5-index-data>`_
 23021	    to binary."""
 23022	
 23023	    def __init__(self, items, strings, parent, isCFF2=None):
 23024	        if isCFF2 is None and hasattr(parent, "isCFF2"):
 23025	            isCFF2 = parent.isCFF2
 23026	            assert isCFF2 is not None
 23027	        self.isCFF2 = isCFF2
 23028	        self.items = self.getItems(items, strings)
 23029	        self.parent = parent
 23030	
 23031	    def getItems(self, items, strings):
 23032	        return items
 23033	
 23034	    def getOffsets(self):
 23035	        # An empty INDEX contains only the count field.
 23036	        if self.items:
 23037	            pos = 1
 23038	            offsets = [pos]
 23039	            for item in self.items:
 23040	                if hasattr(item, "getDataLength"):
 23041	                    pos = pos + item.getDataLength()
 23042	                else:
 23043	                    pos = pos + len(item)
 23044	                offsets.append(pos)
 23045	        else:
 23046	            offsets = []
 23047	        return offsets
 23048	
 23049	    def getDataLength(self):
 23050	        if self.isCFF2:
 23051	            countSize = 4
 23052	        else:
 23053	            countSize = 2
 23054	
 23055	        if self.items:
 23056	            lastOffset = self.getOffsets()[-1]
 23057	            offSize = calcOffSize(lastOffset)
 23058	            dataLength = (
 23059	                countSize
 23060	                + 1  # count
 23061	                + (len(self.items) + 1) * offSize  # offSize
 23062	                + lastOffset  # the offsets
 23063	                - 1  # size of object data
 23064	            )
 23065	        else:
 23066	            # count. For empty INDEX tables, this is the only entry.
 23067	            dataLength = countSize
 23068	
 23069	        return dataLength
 23070	
 23071	    def toFile(self, file):
 23072	        offsets = self.getOffsets()
 23073	        if self.isCFF2:
 23074	            writeCard32(file, len(self.items))
 23075	        else:
 23076	            writeCard16(file, len(self.items))
 23077	        # An empty INDEX contains only the count field.
 23078	        if self.items:
 23079	            offSize = calcOffSize(offsets[-1])
 23080	            writeCard8(file, offSize)
 23081	            offSize = -offSize
 23082	            pack = struct.pack
 23083	            for offset in offsets:
 23084	                binOffset = pack(">l", offset)[offSize:]
 23085	                assert len(binOffset) == -offSize
 23086	                file.write(binOffset)
 23087	            for item in self.items:
 23088	                if hasattr(item, "toFile"):
 23089	                    item.toFile(file)
 23090	                else:
 23091	                    data = tobytes(item, encoding="latin1")
 23092	                    file.write(data)

 23213	class Index(object):
 23214	    """This class represents what the CFF spec calls an INDEX (an array of
 23215	    variable-sized objects). `Index` items can be addressed and set using
 23216	    Python list indexing."""
 23217	
 23218	    compilerClass = IndexCompiler
 23219	
 23220	    def __init__(self, file=None, isCFF2=None):
 23221	        self.items = []
 23222	        self.offsets = offsets = []
 23223	        name = self.__class__.__name__
 23224	        if file is None:
 23225	            return
 23226	        self._isCFF2 = isCFF2
 23227	        log.log(DEBUG, "loading %s at %s", name, file.tell())
 23228	        self.file = file
 23229	        if isCFF2:
 23230	            count = readCard32(file)
 23231	        else:
 23232	            count = readCard16(file)
 23233	        if count == 0:
 23234	            return
 23235	        self.items = [None] * count
 23236	        offSize = readCard8(file)
 23237	        log.log(DEBUG, "    index count: %s offSize: %s", count, offSize)
 23238	        assert offSize <= 4, "offSize too large: %s" % offSize
 23239	        pad = b"\0" * (4 - offSize)
 23240	        for index in range(count + 1):
 23241	            chunk = file.read(offSize)
 23242	            chunk = pad + chunk
 23243	            (offset,) = struct.unpack(">L", chunk)
 23244	            offsets.append(int(offset))
 23245	        self.offsetBase = file.tell() - 1
 23246	        file.seek(self.offsetBase + offsets[-1])  # pretend we've read the whole lot
 23247	        log.log(DEBUG, "    end of %s at %s", name, file.tell())
 23248	
 23249	    def __len__(self):
 23250	        return len(self.items)
 23251	
 23252	    def __getitem__(self, index):
 23253	        item = self.items[index]
 23254	        if item is not None:
 23255	            return item
 23256	        offset = self.offsets[index] + self.offsetBase
 23257	        size = self.offsets[index + 1] - self.offsets[index]
 23258	        file = self.file
 23259	        file.seek(offset)
 23260	        data = file.read(size)
 23261	        assert len(data) == size
 23262	        item = self.produceItem(index, data, file, offset)
 23263	        self.items[index] = item
 23264	        return item
 23265	
 23266	    def __setitem__(self, index, item):
 23267	        self.items[index] = item
 23268	
 23269	    def produceItem(self, index, data, file, offset):
 23270	        return data
 23271	
 23272	    def append(self, item):
 23273	        """Add an item to an INDEX."""
 23274	        self.items.append(item)
 23275	
 23276	    def getCompiler(self, strings, parent, isCFF2=None):
 23277	        return self.compilerClass(self, strings, parent, isCFF2=isCFF2)
 23278	
 23279	    def clear(self):
 23280	        """Empty the INDEX."""
 23281	        del self.items[:]

 24864	    def arg_delta_blend(self, value):
 24865	        """A delta list with blend lists has to be *all* blend lists.
 24866	
 24867	        The value is a list is arranged as follows::
 24868	
 24869	                [
 24870	                        [V0, d0..dn]
 24871	                        [V1, d0..dn]
 24872	                        ...
 24873	                        [Vm, d0..dn]
 24874	                ]
 24875	
 24876	        ``V`` is the absolute coordinate value from the default font, and ``d0-dn``
 24877	        are the delta values from the *n* regions. Each ``V`` is an absolute
 24878	        coordinate from the default font.
 24879	
 24880	        We want to return a list::
 24881	
 24882	                [
 24883	                        [v0, v1..vm]
 24884	                        [d0..dn]
 24885	                        ...
 24886	                        [d0..dn]
 24887	                        numBlends
 24888	                        blendOp
 24889	                ]
 24890	
 24891	        where each ``v`` is relative to the previous default font value.
 24892	        """
 24893	        numMasters = len(value[0])
 24894	        numBlends = len(value)
 24895	        numStack = (numBlends * numMasters) + 1
 24896	        if numStack > self.maxBlendStack:
 24897	            # Figure out the max number of value we can blend
 24898	            # and divide this list up into chunks of that size.
 24899	
 24900	            numBlendValues = int((self.maxBlendStack - 1) / numMasters)
 24901	            out = []
 24902	            while True:
 24903	                numVal = min(len(value), numBlendValues)
 24904	                if numVal == 0:
 24905	                    break
 24906	                valList = value[0:numVal]
 24907	                out1 = self.arg_delta_blend(valList)
 24908	                out.extend(out1)
 24909	                value = value[numVal:]
 24910	        else:
 24911	            firstList = [0] * numBlends
 24912	            deltaList = [None] * numBlends
 24913	            i = 0
 24914	            prevVal = 0
 24915	            while i < numBlends:
 24916	                # For PrivateDict BlueValues, the default font
 24917	                # values are absolute, not relative.
 24918	                # Must convert these back to relative coordinates
 24919	                # before writing to CFF2.
 24920	                defaultValue = value[i][0]
 24921	                firstList[i] = defaultValue - prevVal
 24922	                prevVal = defaultValue
 24923	                deltaList[i] = value[i][1:]
 24924	                i += 1
 24925	
 24926	            relValueList = firstList
 24927	            for blendList in deltaList:
 24928	                relValueList.extend(blendList)
 24929	            out = [encodeNumber(val) for val in relValueList]
 24930	            out.append(encodeNumber(numBlends))
 24931	            out.append(bytechr(blendOp))
 24932	        return out

 25247	class FontDict(BaseDict):

 25249	    # Since fonttools used to pass a lot of fields that are not relevant in the FDArray

 25252	    # values. These are not actually illegal in the context of an FDArray FontDict - you
 25253	    # can legally, per spec, put any arbitrary key/value pair in a FontDict - but are
 25254	    # useless since current major company CFF interpreters ignore anything but the set
 25255	    # listed in this file. So, we just silently skip them. An exception is Weight: this
 25256	    # is not used by any interpreter, but some foundries have asked that this be
 25257	    # supported in FDArray FontDicts just to preserve information about the design when

 26316	class BuildCallback(enum.Enum):
 26317	    """Keyed on (BEFORE_BUILD, class[, Format if available]).
 26318	    Receives (dest, source).
 26319	    Should return (dest, source), which can be new objects.
 26320	    """
 26321	
 26322	    BEFORE_BUILD = enum.auto()
 26323	
 26324	    """Keyed on (AFTER_BUILD, class[, Format if available]).
 26325	    Receives (dest).
 26326	    Should return dest, which can be a new object.
 26327	    """
 26328	    AFTER_BUILD = enum.auto()
 26329	
 26330	    """Keyed on (CREATE_DEFAULT, class[, Format if available]).
 26331	    Receives no arguments.
 26332	    Should return a new instance of class.
 26333	    """

 26337	def _assignable(convertersByName):
 26338	    return {k: v for k, v in convertersByName.items() if not isinstance(v, ComputedInt)}
 26339	
 26340	
 26341	def _isNonStrSequence(value):
 26342	    return isinstance(value, collections.abc.Sequence) and not isinstance(value, str)
 26343	
 26344	
 26345	def _split_format(cls, source):
 26346	    if _isNonStrSequence(source):
 26347	        assert len(source) > 0, f"{cls} needs at least format from {source}"
 26348	        fmt, remainder = source[0], source[1:]
 26349	    elif isinstance(source, collections.abc.Mapping):
 26350	        assert "Format" in source, f"{cls} needs at least Format from {source}"
 26351	        remainder = source.copy()
 26352	        fmt = remainder.pop("Format")
 26353	    else:
 26354	        raise ValueError(f"Not sure how to populate {cls} from {source}")
 26355	
 26356	    assert isinstance(
 26357	        fmt, collections.abc.Hashable
 26358	    ), f"{cls} Format is not hashable: {fmt!r}"
 26359	    assert fmt in cls.convertersByName, f"{cls} invalid Format: {fmt!r}"
 26360	
 26361	    return fmt, remainder

 26364	class TableBuilder:
 26365	    """
 26366	    Helps to populate things derived from BaseTable from maps, tuples, etc.
 26367	
 26368	    A table of lifecycle callbacks may be provided to add logic beyond what is possible
 26369	    based on otData info for the target class. See BuildCallbacks.
 26370	    """
 26371	
 26372	    def __init__(self, callbackTable=None):
 26373	        if callbackTable is None:
 26374	            callbackTable = {}
 26375	        self._callbackTable = callbackTable
 26376	
 26377	    def _convert(self, dest, field, converter, value):
 26378	        enumClass = getattr(converter, "enumClass", None)
 26379	
 26380	        if enumClass:
 26381	            if isinstance(value, enumClass):
 26382	                pass
 26383	            elif isinstance(value, str):
 26384	                try:
 26385	                    value = getattr(enumClass, value.upper())
 26386	                except AttributeError:
 26387	                    raise ValueError(f"{value} is not a valid {enumClass}")
 26388	            else:
 26389	                value = enumClass(value)
 26390	
 26391	        elif isinstance(converter, IntValue):
 26392	            value = otRound(value)
 26393	        elif isinstance(converter, FloatValue):
 26394	            value = float(value)
 26395	
 26396	        elif isinstance(converter, Struct):
 26397	            if converter.repeat:
 26398	                if _isNonStrSequence(value):
 26399	                    value = [self.build(converter.tableClass, v) for v in value]
 26400	                else:
 26401	                    value = [self.build(converter.tableClass, value)]
 26402	                setattr(dest, converter.repeat, len(value))
 26403	            else:
 26404	                value = self.build(converter.tableClass, value)
 26405	        elif callable(converter):
 26406	            value = converter(value)
 26407	
 26408	        setattr(dest, field, value)
 26409	
 26410	    def build(self, cls, source):
 26411	        assert issubclass(cls, BaseTable)
 26412	
 26413	        if isinstance(source, cls):
 26414	            return source
 26415	
 26416	        callbackKey = (cls,)
 26417	        fmt = None
 26418	        if issubclass(cls, FormatSwitchingBaseTable):
 26419	            fmt, source = _split_format(cls, source)
 26420	            callbackKey = (cls, fmt)
 26421	
 26422	        dest = self._callbackTable.get(
 26423	            (BuildCallback.CREATE_DEFAULT,) + callbackKey, lambda: cls()
 26424	        )()
 26425	        assert isinstance(dest, cls)
 26426	
 26427	        convByName = _assignable(cls.convertersByName)
 26428	        skippedFields = set()
 26429	
 26430	        # For format switchers we need to resolve converters based on format
 26431	        if issubclass(cls, FormatSwitchingBaseTable):
 26432	            dest.Format = fmt
 26433	            convByName = _assignable(convByName[dest.Format])
 26434	            skippedFields.add("Format")
 26435	
 26436	        # Convert sequence => mapping so before thunk only has to handle one format
 26437	        if _isNonStrSequence(source):
 26438	            # Sequence (typically list or tuple) assumed to match fields in declaration order
 26439	            assert len(source) <= len(
 26440	                convByName
 26441	            ), f"Sequence of {len(source)} too long for {cls}; expected <= {len(convByName)} values"
 26442	            source = dict(zip(convByName.keys(), source))
 26443	
 26444	        dest, source = self._callbackTable.get(
 26445	            (BuildCallback.BEFORE_BUILD,) + callbackKey, lambda d, s: (d, s)
 26446	        )(dest, source)
 26447	
 26448	        if isinstance(source, collections.abc.Mapping):
 26449	            for field, value in source.items():
 26450	                if field in skippedFields:
 26451	                    continue
 26452	                converter = convByName.get(field, None)
 26453	                if not converter:
 26454	                    raise ValueError(
 26455	                        f"Unrecognized field {field} for {cls}; expected one of {sorted(convByName.keys())}"
 26456	                    )
 26457	                self._convert(dest, field, converter, value)
 26458	        else:
 26459	            # let's try as a 1-tuple
 26460	            dest = self.build(cls, (source,))
 26461	
 26462	        for field, conv in convByName.items():
 26463	            if not hasattr(dest, field) and isinstance(conv, OptionalValue):
 26464	                setattr(dest, field, conv.DEFAULT)
 26465	
 26466	        dest = self._callbackTable.get(
 26467	            (BuildCallback.AFTER_BUILD,) + callbackKey, lambda d: d
 26468	        )(dest)
 26469	
 26470	        return dest

 26473	class TableUnbuilder:
 26474	    def __init__(self, callbackTable=None):
 26475	        if callbackTable is None:
 26476	            callbackTable = {}
 26477	        self._callbackTable = callbackTable
 26478	
 26479	    def unbuild(self, table):
 26480	        assert isinstance(table, BaseTable)
 26481	
 26482	        source = {}
 26483	
 26484	        callbackKey = (type(table),)
 26485	        if isinstance(table, FormatSwitchingBaseTable):
 26486	            source["Format"] = int(table.Format)
 26487	            callbackKey += (table.Format,)
 26488	
 26489	        for converter in table.getConverters():
 26490	            if isinstance(converter, ComputedInt):
 26491	                continue
 26492	            value = getattr(table, converter.name)
 26493	
 26494	            enumClass = getattr(converter, "enumClass", None)
 26495	            if enumClass:
 26496	                source[converter.name] = value.name.lower()
 26497	            elif isinstance(converter, Struct):
 26498	                if converter.repeat:
 26499	                    source[converter.name] = [self.unbuild(v) for v in value]
 26500	                else:
 26501	                    source[converter.name] = self.unbuild(value)
 26502	            elif isinstance(converter, SimpleValue):
 26503	                # "simple" values (e.g. int, float, str) need no further un-building
 26504	                source[converter.name] = value
 26505	            else:
 26506	                raise NotImplementedError(
 26507	                    "Don't know how unbuild {value!r} with {converter!r}"
 26508	                )
 26509	
 26510	        source = self._callbackTable.get(callbackKey, lambda s: s)(source)
 26511	
 26512	        return source

 26741	class GlyphClass(Expression):
 26742	    """A glyph class, such as ``[acute cedilla grave]``."""
 26743	
 26744	    def __init__(self, glyphs=None, location=None):
 26745	        Expression.__init__(self, location)
 26746	        #: The list of glyphs in this class, as :class:`GlyphName` objects.
 26747	        self.glyphs = glyphs if glyphs is not None else []
 26748	        self.original = []
 26749	        self.curr = 0
 26750	
 26751	    def glyphSet(self):
 26752	        """The glyphs in this class as a tuple of :class:`GlyphName` objects."""
 26753	        return tuple(self.glyphs)
 26754	
 26755	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 26756	        if len(self.original):
 26757	            if self.curr < len(self.glyphs):
 26758	                self.original.extend(self.glyphs[self.curr :])
 26759	                self.curr = len(self.glyphs)
 26760	            return "[" + " ".join(map(asFea, self.original)) + "]"
 26761	        else:
 26762	            return "[" + " ".join(map(asFea, self.glyphs)) + "]"
 26763	
 26764	    def extend(self, glyphs):
 26765	        """Add a list of :class:`GlyphName` objects to the class."""
 26766	        self.glyphs.extend(glyphs)
 26767	
 26768	    def append(self, glyph):
 26769	        """Add a single :class:`GlyphName` object to the class."""
 26770	        self.glyphs.append(glyph)
 26771	
 26772	    def add_range(self, start, end, glyphs):
 26773	        """Add a range (e.g. ``A-Z``) to the class. ``start`` and ``end``
 26774	        are either :class:`GlyphName` objects or strings representing the
 26775	        start and end glyphs in the class, and ``glyphs`` is the full list of
 26776	        :class:`GlyphName` objects in the range."""
 26777	        if self.curr < len(self.glyphs):
 26778	            self.original.extend(self.glyphs[self.curr :])
 26779	        self.original.append((start, end))
 26780	        self.glyphs.extend(glyphs)
 26781	        self.curr = len(self.glyphs)
 26782	
 26783	    def add_cid_range(self, start, end, glyphs):
 26784	        """Add a range to the class by glyph ID. ``start`` and ``end`` are the
 26785	        initial and final IDs, and ``glyphs`` is the full list of
 26786	        :class:`GlyphName` objects in the range."""
 26787	        if self.curr < len(self.glyphs):
 26788	            self.original.extend(self.glyphs[self.curr :])
 26789	        self.original.append(("\\{}".format(start), "\\{}".format(end)))
 26790	        self.glyphs.extend(glyphs)
 26791	        self.curr = len(self.glyphs)
 26792	
 26793	    def add_class(self, gc):
 26794	        """Add glyphs from the given :class:`GlyphClassName` object to the
 26795	        class."""
 26796	        if self.curr < len(self.glyphs):
 26797	            self.original.extend(self.glyphs[self.curr :])
 26798	        self.original.append(gc)
 26799	        self.glyphs.extend(gc.glyphSet())
 26800	        self.curr = len(self.glyphs)

 26887	class FeatureBlock(Block):
 26888	    """A named feature block."""
 26889	
 26890	    def __init__(self, name, use_extension=False, location=None):
 26891	        Block.__init__(self, location)
 26892	        self.name, self.use_extension = name, use_extension
 26893	
 26894	    def build(self, builder):
 26895	        """Call the ``start_feature`` callback on the builder object, visit
 26896	        all the statements in this feature, and then call ``end_feature``."""
 26897	        # TODO(sascha): Handle use_extension.
 26898	        builder.start_feature(self.location, self.name)
 26899	        # language exclude_dflt statements modify builder.features_
 26900	        # limit them to this block with temporary builder.features_
 26901	        features = builder.features_
 26902	        builder.features_ = {}
 26903	        Block.build(self, builder)
 26904	        for key, value in builder.features_.items():
 26905	            features.setdefault(key, []).extend(value)
 26906	        builder.features_ = features
 26907	        builder.end_feature()
 26908	
 26909	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 26910	        res = indent + "feature %s " % self.name.strip()
 26911	        if self.use_extension:
 26912	            res += "useExtension "
 26913	        res += "{\n"
 26914	        res += Block.asFea(self, indent=indent)
 26915	        res += indent + "} %s;\n" % self.name.strip()
 26916	        return res

 27023	class MarkClass(object):
 27024	    """One `or more` ``markClass`` statements for the same mark class.
 27025	
 27026	    While glyph classes can be defined only once, the feature file format
 27027	    allows expanding mark classes with multiple definitions, each using
 27028	    different glyphs and anchors. The following are two ``MarkClassDefinitions``
 27029	    for the same ``MarkClass``::
 27030	
 27031	        markClass [acute grave] <anchor 350 800> @FRENCH_ACCENTS;
 27032	        markClass [cedilla] <anchor 350 -200> @FRENCH_ACCENTS;
 27033	
 27034	    The ``MarkClass`` object is therefore just a container for a list of
 27035	    :class:`MarkClassDefinition` statements.
 27036	    """
 27037	
 27038	    def __init__(self, name):
 27039	        self.name = name
 27040	        self.definitions = []
 27041	        self.glyphs = OrderedDict()  # glyph --> ast.MarkClassDefinitions
 27042	
 27043	    def addDefinition(self, definition):
 27044	        """Add a :class:`MarkClassDefinition` statement to this mark class."""
 27045	        assert isinstance(definition, MarkClassDefinition)
 27046	        self.definitions.append(definition)
 27047	        for glyph in definition.glyphSet():
 27048	            if glyph in self.glyphs:
 27049	                otherLoc = self.glyphs[glyph].location
 27050	                if otherLoc is None:
 27051	                    end = ""
 27052	                else:
 27053	                    end = f" at {otherLoc}"
 27054	                raise FeatureLibError(
 27055	                    "Glyph %s already defined%s" % (glyph, end), definition.location
 27056	                )
 27057	            self.glyphs[glyph] = definition
 27058	
 27059	    def glyphSet(self):
 27060	        """The glyphs in this class as a tuple of :class:`GlyphName` objects."""
 27061	        return tuple(self.glyphs.keys())
 27062	
 27063	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 27064	        res = "\n".join(d.asFea() for d in self.definitions)
 27065	        return res

 27068	class MarkClassDefinition(Statement):
 27069	    """A single ``markClass`` statement. The ``markClass`` should be a
 27070	    :class:`MarkClass` object, the ``anchor`` an :class:`Anchor` object,
 27071	    and the ``glyphs`` parameter should be a `glyph-containing object`_ .
 27072	
 27073	    Example:
 27074	
 27075	        .. code:: python
 27076	
 27077	            mc = MarkClass("FRENCH_ACCENTS")
 27078	            mc.addDefinition( MarkClassDefinition(mc, Anchor(350, 800),
 27079	                GlyphClass([ GlyphName("acute"), GlyphName("grave") ])
 27080	            ) )
 27081	            mc.addDefinition( MarkClassDefinition(mc, Anchor(350, -200),
 27082	                GlyphClass([ GlyphName("cedilla") ])
 27083	            ) )
 27084	
 27085	            mc.asFea()
 27086	            # markClass [acute grave] <anchor 350 800> @FRENCH_ACCENTS;
 27087	            # markClass [cedilla] <anchor 350 -200> @FRENCH_ACCENTS;
 27088	
 27089	    """
 27090	
 27091	    def __init__(self, markClass, anchor, glyphs, location=None):
 27092	        Statement.__init__(self, location)
 27093	        assert isinstance(markClass, MarkClass)
 27094	        assert isinstance(anchor, Anchor) and isinstance(glyphs, Expression)
 27095	        self.markClass, self.anchor, self.glyphs = markClass, anchor, glyphs

 27107	class AlternateSubstStatement(Statement):
 27108	    """A ``sub ... from ...`` statement.
 27109	
 27110	    ``prefix``, ``glyph``, ``suffix`` and ``replacement`` should be lists of
 27111	    `glyph-containing objects`_. ``glyph`` should be a `one element list`."""
 27112	
 27113	    def __init__(self, prefix, glyph, suffix, replacement, location=None):
 27114	        Statement.__init__(self, location)
 27115	        self.prefix, self.glyph, self.suffix = (prefix, glyph, suffix)
 27116	        self.replacement = replacement
 27117	
 27118	    def build(self, builder):
 27119	        """Calls the builder's ``add_alternate_subst`` callback."""
 27120	        glyph = self.glyph.glyphSet()
 27121	        assert len(glyph) == 1, glyph
 27122	        glyph = list(glyph)[0]
 27123	        prefix = [p.glyphSet() for p in self.prefix]
 27124	        suffix = [s.glyphSet() for s in self.suffix]
 27125	        replacement = self.replacement.glyphSet()
 27126	        builder.add_alternate_subst(self.location, prefix, glyph, suffix, replacement)
 27127	
 27128	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 27129	        res = "sub "
 27130	        if len(self.prefix) or len(self.suffix):
 27131	            if len(self.prefix):
 27132	                res += " ".join(map(asFea, self.prefix)) + " "

 27234	            if lookup:
 27235	                try:
 27236	                    (_ for _ in lookup)
 27237	                except TypeError:

 27246	            self.location, prefix, glyphs, suffix, self.lookups
 27247	        )

 27250	        res = "pos "

 27252	            len(self.prefix)

 27255	        ):

 27747	class MultipleSubstStatement(Statement):
 27748	    """A multiple substitution statement.
 27749	
 27750	    Args:
 27751	        prefix: a list of `glyph-containing objects`_.
 27752	        glyph: a single glyph-containing object.
 27753	        suffix: a list of glyph-containing objects.
 27754	        replacement: a list of glyph-containing objects.
 27755	        forceChain: If true, the statement is expressed as a chaining rule
 27756	            (e.g. ``sub f' i' by f_i``) even when no context is given.
 27757	    """
 27758	
 27759	    def __init__(
 27760	        self, prefix, glyph, suffix, replacement, forceChain=False, location=None
 27761	    ):
 27762	        Statement.__init__(self, location)
 27763	        self.prefix, self.glyph, self.suffix = prefix, glyph, suffix
 27764	        self.replacement = replacement
 27765	        self.forceChain = forceChain
 27766	
 27767	    def build(self, builder):
 27768	        """Calls the builder object's ``add_multiple_subst`` callback."""
 27769	        prefix = [p.glyphSet() for p in self.prefix]
 27770	        suffix = [s.glyphSet() for s in self.suffix]
 27771	        if hasattr(self.glyph, "glyphSet"):
 27772	            originals = self.glyph.glyphSet()
 27773	        else:
 27774	            originals = [self.glyph]
 27775	        count = len(originals)
 27776	        replaces = []
 27777	        for r in self.replacement:
 27778	            if hasattr(r, "glyphSet"):
 27779	                replace = r.glyphSet()
 27780	            else:
 27781	                replace = [r]
 27782	            if len(replace) == 1 and len(replace) != count:
 27783	                replace = replace * count
 27784	            replaces.append(replace)
 27785	        replaces = list(zip(*replaces))
 27786	
 27787	        seen_originals = set()
 27788	        for i, original in enumerate(originals):
 27789	            if original not in seen_originals:
 27790	                seen_originals.add(original)
 27791	                builder.add_multiple_subst(
 27792	                    self.location,
 27793	                    prefix,
 27794	                    original,
 27795	                    suffix,
 27796	                    replaces and replaces[i] or (),
 27797	                    self.forceChain,
 27798	                )
 27799	
 27800	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 27801	        res = "sub "
 27802	        if len(self.prefix) or len(self.suffix) or self.forceChain:
 27803	            if len(self.prefix):
 27804	                res += " ".join(map(asFea, self.prefix)) + " "
 27805	            res += asFea(self.glyph) + "'"
 27806	            if len(self.suffix):
 27807	                res += " " + " ".join(map(asFea, self.suffix))
 27808	        else:
 27809	            res += asFea(self.glyph)
 27810	        replacement = self.replacement or [NullGlyph()]
 27811	        res += " by "
 27812	        res += " ".join(map(asFea, replacement))
 27813	        res += ";"
 27814	        return res

 27817	class PairPosStatement(Statement):
 27818	    """A pair positioning statement.
 27819	
 27820	    ``glyphs1`` and ``glyphs2`` should be `glyph-containing objects`_.
 27821	    ``valuerecord1`` should be a :class:`ValueRecord` object;
 27822	    ``valuerecord2`` should be either a :class:`ValueRecord` object or ``None``.
 27823	    If ``enumerated`` is true, then this is expressed as an
 27824	    `enumerated pair <https://adobe-type-tools.github.io/afdko/OpenTypeFeatureFileSpecification.html#6.b.ii>`_.
 27825	    """
 27826	
 27827	    def __init__(
 27828	        self,
 27829	        glyphs1,
 27830	        valuerecord1,
 27831	        glyphs2,
 27832	        valuerecord2,
 27833	        enumerated=False,
 27834	        location=None,
 27835	    ):
 27836	        Statement.__init__(self, location)
 27837	        self.enumerated = enumerated
 27838	        self.glyphs1, self.valuerecord1 = glyphs1, valuerecord1
 27839	        self.glyphs2, self.valuerecord2 = glyphs2, valuerecord2
 27840	
 27841	    def build(self, builder):
 27842	        """Calls a callback on the builder object:
 27843	
 27844	        * If the rule is enumerated, calls ``add_specific_pair_pos`` on each
 27845	          combination of first and second glyphs.
 27846	        * If the glyphs are both single :class:`GlyphName` objects, calls
 27847	          ``add_specific_pair_pos``.
 27848	        * Else, calls ``add_class_pair_pos``.
 27849	        """
 27850	        if self.enumerated:
 27851	            g = [self.glyphs1.glyphSet(), self.glyphs2.glyphSet()]
 27852	            seen_pair = False
 27853	            for glyph1, glyph2 in itertools.product(*g):
 27854	                seen_pair = True
 27855	                builder.add_specific_pair_pos(
 27856	                    self.location, glyph1, self.valuerecord1, glyph2, self.valuerecord2
 27857	                )
 27858	            if not seen_pair:
 27859	                raise FeatureLibError(
 27860	                    "Empty glyph class in positioning rule", self.location
 27861	                )
 27862	            return
 27863	
 27864	        is_specific = isinstance(self.glyphs1, GlyphName) and isinstance(
 27865	            self.glyphs2, GlyphName
 27866	        )
 27867	        if is_specific:
 27868	            builder.add_specific_pair_pos(
 27869	                self.location,
 27870	                self.glyphs1.glyph,
 27871	                self.valuerecord1,
 27872	                self.glyphs2.glyph,
 27873	                self.valuerecord2,
 27874	            )
 27875	        else:
 27876	            builder.add_class_pair_pos(
 27877	                self.location,
 27878	                self.glyphs1.glyphSet(),
 27879	                self.valuerecord1,
 27880	                self.glyphs2.glyphSet(),
 27881	                self.valuerecord2,
 27882	            )
 27883	
 27884	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 27885	        res = "enum " if self.enumerated else ""
 27886	        if self.valuerecord2:
 27887	            res += "pos {} {} {} {};".format(
 27888	                self.glyphs1.asFea(),
 27889	                self.valuerecord1.asFea(),
 27890	                self.glyphs2.asFea(),
 27891	                self.valuerecord2.asFea(),
 27892	            )
 27893	        else:
 27894	            res += "pos {} {} {};".format(
 27895	                self.glyphs1.asFea(), self.glyphs2.asFea(), self.valuerecord1.asFea()
 27896	            )
 27897	        return res

 28058	    def __init__(
 28059	        self,
 28060	        xPlacement=None,
 28061	        yPlacement=None,
 28062	        xAdvance=None,
 28063	        yAdvance=None,
 28064	        xPlaDevice=None,
 28065	        yPlaDevice=None,
 28066	        xAdvDevice=None,
 28067	        yAdvDevice=None,

 28072	        self.xPlacement, self.yPlacement = (xPlacement, yPlacement)
 28073	        self.xAdvance, self.yAdvance = (xAdvance, yAdvance)
 28074	        self.xPlaDevice, self.yPlaDevice = (xPlaDevice, yPlaDevice)
 28075	        self.xAdvDevice, self.yAdvDevice = (xAdvDevice, yAdvDevice)
 28076	        self.vertical = vertical
 28077	
 28078	    def __eq__(self, other):
 28079	        return (
 28080	            self.xPlacement == other.xPlacement
 28081	            and self.yPlacement == other.yPlacement
 28082	            and self.xAdvance == other.xAdvance
 28083	            and self.yAdvance == other.yAdvance
 28084	            and self.xPlaDevice == other.xPlaDevice
 28085	            and self.xAdvDevice == other.xAdvDevice
 28086	        )

 28089	        return not self.__eq__(other)

 28092	        return (
 28093	            hash(self.xPlacement)
 28094	            ^ hash(self.yPlacement)
 28095	            ^ hash(self.xAdvance)
 28096	            ^ hash(self.yAdvance)
 28097	            ^ hash(self.xPlaDevice)
 28098	            ^ hash(self.yPlaDevice)
 28099	            ^ hash(self.xAdvDevice)
 28100	            ^ hash(self.yAdvDevice)
 28101	        )

 28104	        if not self:
 28105	            return "<NULL>"
 28106	
 28107	        x, y = self.xPlacement, self.yPlacement
 28108	        xAdvance, yAdvance = self.xAdvance, self.yAdvance
 28109	        xPlaDevice, yPlaDevice = self.xPlaDevice, self.yPlaDevice
 28110	        xAdvDevice, yAdvDevice = self.xAdvDevice, self.yAdvDevice
 28111	        vertical = self.vertical
 28112

 28124	        yAdvance = yAdvance or 0

 28186	class NameRecord(Statement):
 28187	    """Represents a name record. (`Section 9.e. <https://adobe-type-tools.github.io/afdko/OpenTypeFeatureFileSpecification.html#9.e>`_)"""
 28188	
 28189	    def __init__(self, nameID, platformID, platEncID, langID, string, location=None):
 28190	        Statement.__init__(self, location)
 28191	        self.nameID = nameID  #: Name ID as integer (e.g. 9 for designer's name)
 28192	        self.platformID = platformID  #: Platform ID as integer
 28193	        self.platEncID = platEncID  #: Platform encoding ID as integer
 28194	        self.langID = langID  #: Language ID as integer
 28195	        self.string = string  #: Name record value
 28196	
 28197	    def build(self, builder):
 28198	        """Calls the builder object's ``add_name_record`` callback."""
 28199	        builder.add_name_record(
 28200	            self.location,
 28201	            self.nameID,
 28202	            self.platformID,
 28203	            self.platEncID,
 28204	            self.langID,
 28205	            self.string,
 28206	        )
 28207	
 28208	    def asFea(self, indent=""):
 28209	        def escape(c, escape_pattern):
 28210	            # Also escape U+0022 QUOTATION MARK and U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS
 28211	            if c >= 0x20 and c <= 0x7E and c not in (0x22, 0x5C):
 28212	                return chr(c)
 28213	            else:
 28214	                return escape_pattern % c
 28215	
 28216	        encoding = getEncoding(self.platformID, self.platEncID, self.langID)
 28217	        if encoding is None:
 28218	            raise FeatureLibError("Unsupported encoding", self.location)
 28219	        s = tobytes(self.string, encoding=encoding)
 28220	        if encoding == "utf_16_be":
 28221	            escaped_string = "".join(
 28222	                [
 28223	                    escape(byteord(s[i]) * 256 + byteord(s[i + 1]), r"\%04x")
 28224	                    for i in range(0, len(s), 2)
 28225	                ]
 28226	            )
 28227	        else:
 28228	            escaped_string = "".join([escape(byteord(b), r"\%02x") for b in s])
 28229	        plat = simplify_name_attributes(self.platformID, self.platEncID, self.langID)
 28230	        if plat != "":
 28231	            plat += " "
 28232	        return 'nameid {} {}"{}";'.format(self.nameID, plat, escaped_string)

 28617	        ):

 28619	                f"variation block used undefined conditionset {self.conditionset}",
 28620	                self.location,
 28621	            )
 28622	
 28623	        # language exclude_dflt statements modify builder.features_
 28624	        # limit them to this block with temporary builder.features_
 28625	        features = builder.features_
 28626	        builder.features_ = {}
 28627	        Block.build(self, builder)
 28628	        for key, value in builder.features_.items():
 28629	            items = builder.feature_variations_.setdefault(key, {}).setdefault(
 28630	                self.conditionset, []
 28631	            )
 28632	            items.extend(value)
 28633	            if key not in features:

 28694	def buildConverters(tableSpec, tableNamespace):
 28695	    """Given a table spec from otData.py, build a converter object for each
 28696	    field of the table. This is called for each table in otData.py, and
 28697	    the results are assigned to the corresponding class in otTables.py."""
 28698	    converters = []
 28699	    convertersByName = {}
 28700	    for tp, name, repeat, aux, descr in tableSpec:
 28701	        tableName = name
 28702	        if name.startswith("ValueFormat"):
 28703	            assert tp == "uint16"
 28704	            converterClass = ValueFormat
 28705	        elif name.endswith("Count") or name in ("StructLength", "MorphType"):
 28706	            converterClass = {
 28707	                "uint8": ComputedUInt8,
 28708	                "uint16": ComputedUShort,
 28709	                "uint32": ComputedULong,
 28710	            }[tp]
 28711	        elif name == "SubTable":
 28712	            converterClass = SubTable
 28713	        elif name == "ExtSubTable":
 28714	            converterClass = ExtSubTable
 28715	        elif name == "SubStruct":
 28716	            converterClass = SubStruct
 28717	        elif name == "FeatureParams":
 28718	            converterClass = FeatureParams
 28719	        elif name in ("CIDGlyphMapping", "GlyphCIDMapping"):
 28720	            converterClass = StructWithLength
 28721	        else:
 28722	            if not tp in converterMapping and "(" not in tp:
 28723	                tableName = tp
 28724	                converterClass = Struct
 28725	            else:
 28726	                converterClass = eval(tp, tableNamespace, converterMapping)
 28727	
 28728	        conv = converterClass(name, repeat, aux, description=descr)
 28729	
 28730	        if conv.tableClass:
 28731	            # A "template" such as OffsetTo(AType) knows the table class already
 28732	            tableClass = conv.tableClass
 28733	        elif tp in ("MortChain", "MortSubtable", "MorxChain"):
 28734	            tableClass = tableNamespace.get(tp)
 28735	        else:
 28736	            tableClass = tableNamespace.get(tableName)
 28737	
 28738	        if not conv.tableClass:
 28739	            conv.tableClass = tableClass
 28740	
 28741	        if name in ["SubTable", "ExtSubTable", "SubStruct"]:
 28742	            conv.lookupTypes = tableNamespace["lookupTypes"]
 28743	            # also create reverse mapping
 28744	            for t in conv.lookupTypes.values():
 28745	                for cls in t.values():
 28746	                    convertersByName[cls.__name__] = Table(name, repeat, aux, cls)
 28747	        if name == "FeatureParams":
 28748	            conv.featureParamTypes = tableNamespace["featureParamTypes"]
 28749	            conv.defaultFeatureParams = tableNamespace["FeatureParams"]
 28750	            for cls in conv.featureParamTypes.values():
 28751	                convertersByName[cls.__name__] = Table(name, repeat, aux, cls)
 28752	        converters.append(conv)
 28753	        assert name not in convertersByName, name
 28754	        convertersByName[name] = conv
 28755	    return converters, convertersByName

 29719	# The AAT 'ankr' table has an unusual structure: An offset to an AATLookup
 29720	# followed by an offset to a glyph data table. Other than usual, the
 29721	# offsets in the AATLookup are not relative to the beginning of
 29722	# the beginning of the 'ankr' table, but relative to the glyph data table.
 29723	# So, to find the anchor data for a glyph, one needs to add the offset
 29724	# to the data table to the offset found in the AATLookup, and then use
 29725	# the sum of these two offsets to find the actual data.
 29726	class AATLookupWithDataOffset(BaseConverter):
 29727	    def read(self, reader, font, tableDict):
 29728	        lookupOffset = reader.readULong()
 29729	        dataOffset = reader.readULong()
 29730	        lookupReader = reader.getSubReader(lookupOffset)
 29731	        lookup = AATLookup("DataOffsets", None, None, UShort)
 29732	        offsets = lookup.read(lookupReader, font, tableDict)
 29733	        result = {}
 29734	        for glyph, offset in offsets.items():
 29735	            dataReader = reader.getSubReader(offset + dataOffset)
 29736	            item = self.tableClass()
 29737	            item.decompile(dataReader, font)
 29738	            result[glyph] = item
 29739	        return result
 29740	
 29741	    def write(self, writer, font, tableDict, value, repeatIndex=None):
 29742	        # We do not work with OTTableWriter sub-writers because
 29743	        # the offsets in our AATLookup are relative to our data
 29744	        # table, for which we need to provide an offset value itself.
 29745	        # It might have been possible to somehow make a kludge for
 29746	        # performing this indirect offset computation directly inside
 29747	        # OTTableWriter. But this would have made the internal logic
 29748	        # of OTTableWriter even more complex than it already is,
 29749	        # so we decided to roll our own offset computation for the
 29750	        # contents of the AATLookup and associated data table.
 29751	        offsetByGlyph, offsetByData, dataLen = {}, {}, 0
 29752	        compiledData = []
 29753	        for glyph in sorted(value, key=font.getGlyphID):
 29754	            subWriter = OTTableWriter()
 29755	            value[glyph].compile(subWriter, font)
 29756	            data = subWriter.getAllData()
 29757	            offset = offsetByData.get(data, None)
 29758	            if offset == None:
 29759	                offset = dataLen
 29760	                dataLen = dataLen + len(data)
 29761	                offsetByData[data] = offset
 29762	                compiledData.append(data)
 29763	            offsetByGlyph[glyph] = offset
 29764	        # For calculating the offsets to our AATLookup and data table,
 29765	        # we can use the regular OTTableWriter infrastructure.
 29766	        lookupWriter = writer.getSubWriter()
 29767	        lookup = AATLookup("DataOffsets", None, None, UShort)
 29768	        lookup.write(lookupWriter, font, tableDict, offsetByGlyph, None)
 29769	
 29770	        dataWriter = writer.getSubWriter()
 29771	        writer.writeSubTable(lookupWriter, offsetSize=4)
 29772	        writer.writeSubTable(dataWriter, offsetSize=4)
 29773	        for d in compiledData:
 29774	            dataWriter.writeData(d)
 29775

 29803	            subtable.TextDirection = "Any"

 29806	        else:
