 29810	        pos = reader.pos
 29811	        m = MorxSubtable()
 29812	        m.StructLength = reader.readULong()
 29813	        flags = reader.readUInt8()
 29814	        orderKey = ((flags & 0x40) != 0, (flags & 0x10) != 0)
 29815	        m.ProcessingOrder = self._PROCESSING_ORDERS[orderKey]
 29816	        self._setTextDirectionFromCoverageFlags(flags, m)
 29817	        m.Reserved = reader.readUShort()
 29818	        m.Reserved |= (flags & 0xF) << 16
 29819	        m.MorphType = reader.readUInt8()
 29820	        m.SubFeatureFlags = reader.readULong()
 29821	        tableClass = lookupTypes["morx"].get(m.MorphType)
 29822	        if tableClass is None:
 29823	            assert False, "unsupported 'morx' lookup type %s" % m.MorphType
 29824	        # To decode AAT ligatures, we need to know the subtable size.
 29825	        # The easiest way to pass this along is to create a new reader
 29826	        # that works on just the subtable as its data.
 29827	        headerLength = reader.pos - pos
 29828	        data = reader.data[reader.pos : reader.pos + m.StructLength - headerLength]
 29829	        assert len(data) == m.StructLength - headerLength
 29830	        subReader = OTTableReader(data=data, tableTag=reader.tableTag)
 29831	        m.SubStruct = tableClass()
 29832	        m.SubStruct.decompile(subReader, font)
 29833	        reader.seek(pos + m.StructLength)
 29834	        return m

 30302	class DeltaValue(BaseConverter):
 30303	    def read(self, reader, font, tableDict):
 30304	        StartSize = tableDict["StartSize"]
 30305	        EndSize = tableDict["EndSize"]
 30306	        DeltaFormat = tableDict["DeltaFormat"]
 30307	        assert DeltaFormat in (1, 2, 3), "illegal DeltaFormat"
 30308	        nItems = EndSize - StartSize + 1
 30309	        nBits = 1 << DeltaFormat
 30310	        minusOffset = 1 << nBits
 30311	        mask = (1 << nBits) - 1
 30312	        signMask = 1 << (nBits - 1)
 30313	
 30314	        DeltaValue = []
 30315	        tmp, shift = 0, 0
 30316	        for i in range(nItems):
 30317	            if shift == 0:
 30318	                tmp, shift = reader.readUShort(), 16
 30319	            shift = shift - nBits
 30320	            value = (tmp >> shift) & mask
 30321	            if value & signMask:
 30322	                value = value - minusOffset
 30323	            DeltaValue.append(value)
 30324	        return DeltaValue
 30325	
 30326	    def write(self, writer, font, tableDict, value, repeatIndex=None):
 30327	        StartSize = tableDict["StartSize"]
 30328	        EndSize = tableDict["EndSize"]
 30329	        DeltaFormat = tableDict["DeltaFormat"]
 30330	        DeltaValue = value
 30331	        assert DeltaFormat in (1, 2, 3), "illegal DeltaFormat"
 30332	        nItems = EndSize - StartSize + 1
 30333	        nBits = 1 << DeltaFormat
 30334	        assert len(DeltaValue) == nItems
 30335	        mask = (1 << nBits) - 1
 30336	
 30337	        tmp, shift = 0, 16
 30338	        for value in DeltaValue:
 30339	            shift = shift - nBits
 30340	            tmp = tmp | ((value & mask) << shift)
 30341	            if shift == 0:
 30342	                writer.writeUShort(tmp)
 30343	                tmp, shift = 0, 16
 30344	        if shift != 16:
 30345	            writer.writeUShort(tmp)

 32027	    def by_priority(self):
 32028	        """
 32029	        Return a dictionary of format objects keyed by (field id and format property).
 32030	        This can be used to map the formats to field but also to dedupe to match
 32031	        worksheet definitions which are grouped by cell range
 32032	        """
 32033	
 32034	        fmts = {}
 32035	        for fmt in self.conditionalFormat:
 32036	            for area in fmt.pivotAreas:
 32037	                for ref in area.references:
 32038	                    for field in ref.x:
 32039	                        key = (field.v, fmt.priority)
 32040	                        fmts[key] = fmt
 32041	
 32042	        return fmts
 32043	
 32044	
 32045	    def _dedupe(self):
 32046	        """
 32047	        Group formats by field index and priority.
 32048	        Sorted to match sorting and grouping for corresponding worksheet formats
 32049	
 32050	        The implemtenters notes contain significant deviance from the OOXML
 32051	        specification, in particular how conditional formats in tables relate to
 32052	        those defined in corresponding worksheets and how to determine which
 32053	        format applies to which fields.
 32054	
 32055	        There are some magical interdependencies:
 32056	
 32057	        * Every pivot table fmt must have a worksheet cxf with the same priority.
 32058	
 32059	        * In the reference part the field 4294967294 refers to a data field, the
 32060	        spec says -2
 32061	
 32062	        * Data fields are referenced by the 0-index reference.x.v value
 32063	
 32064	        Things are made more complicated by the fact that field items behave
 32065	        diffently if the parent is a reference or shared item: "In Office if the
 32066	        parent is the reference element, then restrictions of this value are
 32067	        defined by reference@field. If the parent is the tables element, then
 32068	        this value specifies the index into the table tag position in @url."
 32069	        Yeah, right!
 32070	        """
 32071	        fmts = self.by_priority()
 32072	        # sort by priority in order, keeping the highest numerical priority, least when
 32073	        # actually applied
 32074	        # this is not documented but it's what Excel is happy with
 32075	        fmts = {field:fmt for (field, priority), fmt in sorted(fmts.items(), reverse=True)}
 32076	        #fmts = {field:fmt for (field, priority), fmt in fmts.items()}
 32077	        if fmts:
 32078	            self.conditionalFormat = list(fmts.values())
 32079	
 32080	
 32081	    @property
 32082	    def count(self):
 32083	        return len(self.conditionalFormat)
 32084	
 32085	
 32086	    def to_tree(self, tagname=None):
 32087	        self._dedupe()
 32088	        return super().to_tree(tagname)

 33393	class OWComponent:
 33394	    """
 33395	    Mixin for classes that contain settings and/or attributes that trigger
 33396	    callbacks when changed.
 33397	
 33398	    The class initializes the settings handler, provides `__setattr__` that
 33399	    triggers callbacks, and provides `control` attribute for access to
 33400	    Qt widgets controling particular attributes.
 33401	
 33402	    Callbacks are exploited by controls (e.g. check boxes, line edits,
 33403	    combo boxes...) that are synchronized with attribute values. Changing
 33404	    the value of the attribute triggers a call to a function that updates
 33405	    the Qt widget accordingly.
 33406	
 33407	    The class is mixed into `widget.OWBaseWidget`, and must also be mixed into
 33408	    all widgets not derived from `widget.OWBaseWidget` that contain settings or
 33409	    Qt widgets inserted by function in `orangewidget.gui` module. See
 33410	    `OWScatterPlotGraph` for an example.
 33411	    """
 33412	    def __init__(self, widget=None):
 33413	        self.controlled_attributes = defaultdict(list)
 33414	        self.controls = ControlGetter(self)
 33415	        if widget is not None and widget.settingsHandler:
 33416	            widget.settingsHandler.initialize(self)
 33417	
 33418	    def _reset_settings(self):
 33419	        """
 33420	        Copy default settings to instance's settings. This method can be
 33421	        called from OWWidget's reset_settings, but will mostly have to be
 33422	        followed by calling a method that updates the widget.
 33423	        """
 33424	        self.settingsHandler.reset_to_original(self)
 33425	
 33426	    def connect_control(self, name, func):
 33427	        """
 33428	        Add `func` to the list of functions called when the value of the
 33429	        attribute `name` is set.
 33430	
 33431	        If the name includes a dot, it is assumed that the part the before the
 33432	        first dot is a name of an attribute containing an instance of a
 33433	        component, and the call is transferred to its `conntect_control`. For
 33434	        instance, `calling `obj.connect_control("graph.attr_x", f)` is
 33435	        equivalent to `obj.graph.connect_control("attr_x", f)`.
 33436	
 33437	        Args:
 33438	            name (str): attribute name
 33439	            func (callable): callback function
 33440	        """
 33441	        if "." in name:
 33442	            name, rest = name.split(".", 1)
 33443	            sub = getattr(self, name)
 33444	            sub.connect_control(rest, func)
 33445	        else:
 33446	            self.controlled_attributes[name].append(func)
 33447	
 33448	    def __setattr__(self, name, value):
 33449	        """Set the attribute value and trigger any attached callbacks.
 33450	
 33451	        For backward compatibility, the name can include dots, e.g.
 33452	        `graph.attr_x`. `obj.__setattr__('x.y', v)` is equivalent to
 33453	        `obj.x.__setattr__('x', v)`.
 33454	
 33455	        Args:
 33456	            name (str): attribute name
 33457	            value (object): value to set to the member.
 33458	        """
 33459	        if "." in name:
 33460	            name, rest = name.split(".", 1)
 33461	            sub = getattr(self, name)
 33462	            setattr(sub, rest, value)
 33463	        else:
 33464	            super().__setattr__(name, value)
 33465	            # First check that the widget is not just being constructed
 33466	            if hasattr(self, "controlled_attributes"):
 33467	                for callback in self.controlled_attributes.get(name, ()):
 33468	                    callback(value)

 33472	                addToLayout=True, stretch=0, sizePolicy=None,
 33473	                disabled=False, tooltip=None, disabledBy=None,
 33474	                addSpaceBefore=False, **kwargs):
 33475	    """
 33476	    Helper function that sets various properties of the widget using a common
 33477	    set of arguments.
 33478	
 33479	    The function
 33480	    - sets the `control`'s attribute `box`, if `box` is given and `control.box`
 33481	    is not yet set,
 33482	    - attaches a tool tip to the `control` if specified,
 33483	    - disables the `control`, if `disabled` is set to `True`,
 33484	    - adds the `box` to the `parent`'s layout unless `addToLayout` is set to
 33485	    `False`; the stretch factor can be specified,
 33486	    - adds the control into the box's layout if the box is given (regardless
 33487	    of `addToLayout`!)
 33488	    - sets the size policy for the box or the control, if the policy is given,
 33489	    - adds space in the `parent`'s layout after the `box` if `addSpace` is set
 33490	    and `addToLayout` is not `False`.
 33491	
 33492	    If `box` is the same as `parent` it is set to `None`; this is convenient
 33493	    because of the way complex controls are inserted.

 33496	    function mimic the behaviour of PyQt's constructors. For instance, if
 33497	    `gui.lineEdit` is called with keyword argument `sizePolicy=some_policy`,
 33498	    `miscallenea` will call `control.setSizePolicy(some_policy)`.

 33501	    :type control: QWidget
 33502	    :param box: the box into which the widget was inserted
 33503	    :type box: QWidget or None
 33504	    :param parent: the parent into whose layout the box or the control will be
 33505	        inserted
 33506	    :type parent: QWidget
 33507	    :param addSpaceBefore: the amount of space to add before the widget
 33508	    :type addSpaceBefore: bool or int
 33509	    :param disabled: If set to `True`, the widget is initially disabled
 33510	    :type disabled: bool
 33511	    :param addToLayout: If set to `False` the widget is not added to the layout
 33512	    :type addToLayout: bool
 33513	    :param stretch: the stretch factor for this widget, used when adding to
 33514	        the layout (default: 0)
 33515	    :type stretch: int
 33516	    :param tooltip: tooltip that is attached to the widget
 33517	    :type tooltip: str or None

 33519	    :type disabledBy: QCheckBox or None

 33521	    :type sizePolicy: QSizePolicy
 33522	    """

 33531	        else:

 33796	class SpinBoxMixin:

 33798	    The class overloads :obj:`onChange` event handler to show the commit button,
 33799	    and :obj:`onEnter` to commit the change when enter is pressed.

 33802	    instead of scrolling.

 33805	    valueCommitted = Signal(object)

 33807	    def __init__(self, minv, maxv, step, parent=None, verticalDrag=True):
 33808	        """
 33809	        Construct the object and set the range (`minv`, `maxv`) and the step.
 33810	        :param minv: Minimal value
 33811	        :type minv: int
 33812	        :param maxv: Maximal value
 33813	        :type maxv: int
 33814	        :param step: Step
 33815	        :type step: int

 33817	        :type parent: QWidget

 33819	        :type verticalDrag: bool

 33821	        super().__init__(parent)
 33822	        self.setRange(minv, maxv)
 33823	        self.setSingleStep(step)
 33824	
 33825	        self.equalityChecker = int.__eq__
 33826	
 33827	        self.mouseHeld = False
 33828	        self.verticalDirection = verticalDrag
 33829	        self.mouseStartPos = QtCore.QPoint()
 33830	        self.preDragValue = 0
 33831	
 33832	        self.textEditing = False
 33833	        self.preEditvalue = 0
 33834

 33836	        self.installEventFilter(self)

 33841	        self.setFocusPolicy(Qt.StrongFocus)

 33843	        self.cback = None
 33844	        self.cfunc = None

 33846	    def __onEditingFinished(self):
 33847	        """
 33848	        After user input is finished, commit the new value.
 33849	        """
 33850	        if not self.mouseHeld and not self.textEditing:
 33851	            # value hasn't been altered
 33852	            return
 33853	        if self.mouseHeld:
 33854	            self.mouseHeld = False
 33855	            initialValue = self.preDragValue
 33856	        if self.textEditing:
 33857	            # mouse held can be triggered after editing, but not vice versa
 33858	            self.textEditing = False
 33859	            initialValue = self.preEditvalue
 33860	        value = self.value()
 33861	        if not self.equalityChecker(initialValue, value):
 33862	            # if value has changed, commit it
 33863	            self.__commitValue(value)
 33864	
 33865	    def __onValueChanged(self, value):
 33866	        """
 33867	        When the value is changed outwith user input, commit it.
 33868	        """
 33869	        if not self.mouseHeld and not self.textEditing:
 33870	            self.__commitValue(value)
 33871	
 33872	    def __commitValue(self, value):
 33873	        self.valueCommitted.emit(value)
 33874	        if self.cback:
 33875	            self.cback(value)
 33876	        if self.cfunc:
 33877	            self.cfunc()

 33879	    def eventFilter(self, obj, event):
 33880	        if not self.isEnabled() or \
 33881	                not (isinstance(obj, SpinBoxMixin) or isinstance(obj, QLineEdit)):
 33882	            return super().eventFilter(obj, event)
 33883	
 33884	        cursor = Qt.SizeVerCursor if self.verticalDirection else Qt.SizeHorCursor
 33885	
 33886	        if event.type() == QEvent.MouseButtonPress:
 33887	            # prepare click+drag
 33888	            self.mouseStartPos = event.globalPos()
 33889	            self.preDragValue = self.value()
 33890	            self.mouseHeld = True
 33891	        elif event.type() == QEvent.MouseMove and self.mouseHeld and isinstance(obj, QLineEdit):
 33892	            # do click+drag
 33893	            # override default cursor on drag
 33894	            if QApplication.overrideCursor() != cursor:
 33895	                QApplication.setOverrideCursor(cursor)
 33896	
 33897	            stepSize = self.singleStep()
 33898	
 33899	            pos = event.globalPos()
 33900	            posVal = pos.y() if self.verticalDirection else -pos.x()
 33901	            posValStart = self.mouseStartPos.y() if self.verticalDirection else -self.mouseStartPos.x()
 33902	            diff = posValStart - posVal
 33903	
 33904	            # these magic params are pretty arbitrary, ensure that it's still
 33905	            # possible to easily highlight the text if moving mouse slightly
 33906	            # up/down, with the default stepsize
 33907	            normalizedDiff = abs(diff) / 30
 33908	            exponent = 1 + min(normalizedDiff / 10, 3)
 33909	            valueOffset = int(normalizedDiff ** exponent) * stepSize
 33910	            valueOffset = math.copysign(valueOffset, diff)
 33911	            # Need to preserve the value type
 33912	            valueOffset = type(self.preDragValue)(valueOffset)
 33913	            self.setValue(self.preDragValue + valueOffset)
 33914	
 33915	        elif event.type() == QEvent.MouseButtonRelease:

 33917	            # restore default cursor on release
 33918	            while QApplication.overrideCursor() is not None:
 33919	                QApplication.restoreOverrideCursor()

 33924	            event.ignore()

 33926	        elif event.type() in (QEvent.KeyPress, QEvent.KeyRelease):
 33927	            # handle committing keyboard entry only on editingFinished
 33928	            if self.mouseHeld:
 33929	                # if performing click+drag, ignore key events

 34567	class DelayedNotification(QObject):
 34568	    """
 34569	    A proxy for successive calls/signals that emits a signal
 34570	    only when there are no calls for a given time.
 34571	
 34572	    Also allows for mechanism that prevents successive equivalent calls:
 34573	    ff values are passed to the "changed" method, a signal is only emitted
 34574	    if the last passed values differ from the last passed values at the
 34575	    previous emission.
 34576	    """
 34577	    notification = Signal()
 34578	
 34579	    def __init__(self, parent=None, timeout=500):
 34580	        super().__init__(parent=parent)
 34581	        self.timeout = timeout
 34582	        self._timer = QTimer(self)
 34583	        self._timer.timeout.connect(self.notify_immediately)
 34584	        self._did_notify = False  # if anything was sent at all
 34585	        self._last_value = None  # last value passed to changed
 34586	        self._last_notified = None  # value at the last notification
 34587	
 34588	    def changed(self, *args):
 34589	        self._last_value = args
 34590	        self._timer.start(self.timeout)
 34591	
 34592	    def notify_immediately(self):
 34593	        self._timer.stop()
 34594	        if self._did_notify and self._last_notified == self._last_value:
 34595	            return
 34596	        self._last_notified = self._last_value
 34597	        self._did_notify = True
 34598	        self.notification.emit()

 34981	# Decorator deferred allows for doing this:
 34982	#
 34983	# class MyWidget(OWBaseWidget):
 34984	#    def __init__(self):
 34985	#        ...
 34986	#        # construct some control, for instance a checkbox, which calls
 34987	#        # a deferred commit
 34988	#        cb = gui.checkbox(..., callback=commit.deferred)
 34989	#        ...
 34990	#        gui.auto_commit(..., commit=commit)
 34991	#
 34992	#     @deferred
 34993	#     def commit(self):
 34994	#         ...
 34995	#
 34996	#     def some_method(self):
 34997	#         ...
 34998	#         self.commit.now()
 34999	#
 35000	#     def another_method(self):
 35001	#         ...
 35002	#         self.commit.deferred()
 35003	#
 35004	# Calling self.commit() will raise an exception that one must choose to call
 35005	# either `now` or `deferred`.
 35006	#
 35007	# 1. `now` and `deferred` are created by `gui.auto_commit` and must be
 35008	#    stored to the instance.
 35009	#
 35010	#    Hence, auto_commit stores `now` and `then` into `master.__<name>_data.now`
 35011	#    and`master.<name>_data.deferred`, where <data> is the name of the
 35012	#    decorated method (usually "commit").
 35013	#
 35014	# 2. Calling a decorated self.commit() should raise an exception that one
 35015	#    must choose between `now` and `deferred` ... unless when calling
 35016	#    super().commit() from overriden commit.
 35017	#
 35018	#    Decorator would thus replace the method with a function (or a callable)
 35019	#    that raises an exception ... except for when calling super().
 35020	#
 35021	#    With everything else in place, the only simple way to allow calling super
 35022	#    that I see is to have a flag (..._data.commit_depth) that we're already
 35023	#    within commit.If we're in a commit, we allow calling the decorated commit,
 35024	#    otherwise raise an exception. `commit` is usually not called from multiple
 35025	#    threads, and even if is is, the only consequence would be that we will
 35026	#    (in rare, unfortunate cases with very exact timing) allow calling
 35027	#    self.commit instead of (essentially) self.commit.now instead of raising
 35028	#    a rather diagnostic exception. This is a non-issue.
 35029	#
 35030	# 3. `now` and `deferred` must have a reference to the widget instance
 35031	#    (that is, to what will be bound to `self` in the actual `commit`.
 35032	#
 35033	#    Therefore, we cannot simply have a `commit` to which we attach `now`
 35034	#    and `deferred` because `commit.now` would then be a function - one and the
 35035	#    same function for all widgets of that class, not a method bound to a
 35036	#    particular instance's commit.
 35037	#
 35038	#    To solve this problem, the decorated `commit` is not a function but a
 35039	#    property (of class `DeferrerProperty`) that returns a callable object
 35040	#    (of class `Deferred`). When the property is retrieved, we get a reference
 35041	#    to the instance which is kept in the closure. `Deferred` than provides
 35042	#    `now` and `deferred`.
 35043	
 35044	# 4. Although `now` and `deferred` are constructed only in gui.auto_commit,
 35045	#    they (esp. `deferred`) must by available before that - not for
 35046	#    being called but for being stored as a callback for the checkbox.
 35047	#
 35048	#    To solve this problem, `Deferred` returns either a `..._data.now` and
 35049	#    `..._data.deferred` set by auto_commit; if they are not yet set, it returns
 35050	#    a lambda that calls them, essentially thunking a function that does not
 35051	#    yet exist.
 35052	#
 35053	# 5. `now` and `deferred` are set by `auto_commit` as well as by mocking in
 35054	#    unit tests. Because on the outside we only see commit.now and
 35055	#    commit.deffered (although they are stored elsewhere, not as attributes
 35056	#    of commit), they need to pretend to be attributes. Hence we patch
 35057	#    __setattr__, __getattribute__ and __delattr__.
 35058	
 35059	# The type hint is somewhat wrong: the decorator returns a property, which is
 35060	# a function, but in practice it's the same. PyCharm correctly recognizes it.
 35061	if sys.version_info >= (3, 8):
 35062	    from typing import Protocol
 35063	
 35064	
 35065	    class DeferredFunc(Protocol):
 35066	        def deferred(self) -> None:
 35067	            ...
 35068	
 35069	        def now(self) -> None:
 35070	            ...
 35071	else:
 35072	    from typing import Any
 35073	    DeferredFunc = Any
 35074	
 35075	
 35076	if sys.version_info >= (3, 7):
 35077	    from typing import Optional, Callable
 35078	    from dataclasses import dataclass
 35079	
 35080	    @dataclass
 35081	    class DeferredData:
 35082	        # now and deferred are set by auto_commit
 35083	        now: Optional[Callable] = None
 35084	        deferred: Optional[Callable] = None
 35085	        # if True, data was changed while auto was disabled,
 35086	        # so enabling auto commit must call `func`
 35087	        dirty: bool = False
 35088	        # A flag (counter) telling that we're within commit and
 35089	        # super().commit() should not raise an exception
 35090	        commit_depth: int = 0
 35091	else:
 35092	    class DeferredData:
 35093	        def __init__(self):
 35094	            self.now = self.deferred = None
 35095	            self.dirty = False
 35096	            self.commit_depth = 0
 35097

 35099	def deferred(func) -> DeferredFunc:
 35100	    name = func.__name__
 35101	
 35102	    # Deferred method is turned into a property that returns a class, with
 35103	    # __call__ that raises an exception about being deferred
 35104	
 35105	    class DeferrerProperty:
 35106	        def __get__(self, instance, owner=None):
 35107	            if instance is None:
 35108	                # We come here is somebody retrieves, e.g. OWTable.commit
 35109	                data = None
 35110	            else:
 35111	                # `DeferredData` is created once per instance
 35112	                data = instance.__dict__.setdefault(f"__{name}_data",
 35113	                                                    DeferredData())
 35114	
 35115	            class Deferred:
 35116	                # A property that represents commit. Its closure include
 35117	                # - func: the original commit method
 35118	                # - instance: a widget instance
 35119	                # and, for practicality
 35120	                # - data: a data class containing `now`, `deferred`, `dirty`
 35121	                #         and `commit_depth` for this `instance`
 35122	                # - name: name of the method being decorate (usually "commit")
 35123	
 35124	                # Name of the function being decorated, copied to a standard
 35125	                # attribute; used, for instance, in auto_commit to check for
 35126	                # decorated overriden methods and in exception messages
 35127	                __name__ = name
 35128	
 35129	                # A flag that tells an observer that the method is decorated
 35130	                # auto_commit uses it to check that a widget that overrides
 35131	                # a decorated method also decorates its method
 35132	                decorated = True
 35133	
 35134	                @classmethod
 35135	                def __call__(cls):
 35136	                    # Semantically, decorated method is replaced by this one,
 35137	                    # which raises an exception except in super calls.
 35138	
 35139	                    # If commit_depth > 0, we're calling super (assuming
 35140	                    # no threading on commit!)
 35141	                    if data.commit_depth:
 35142	                        cls.call()
 35143	                    else:
 35144	                        raise RuntimeError(
 35145	                            "This function is deferred; explicitly call "
 35146	                            f"{name}.deferred or {name}.now")
 35147	
 35148	                @staticmethod
 35149	                def call():
 35150	                    data.commit_depth += 1
 35151	                    try:
 35152	                        acting_func = instance.__dict__.get(name, func)
 35153	                        acting_func(instance)
 35154	                    finally:
 35155	                        data.commit_depth -= 1
 35156	
 35157	                def __setattr__(self, key, value):
 35158	                    if key in ("now", "deferred"):
 35159	                        setattr(data, key, value)
 35160	                    else:
 35161	                        super().__setattr__(key, value)
 35162	
 35163	                def __getattribute__(self, key):
 35164	                    if key in ("now", "deferred"):
 35165	                        # If auto_commit already set a function, return it.
 35166	                        # If not, return that function that calls a function,
 35167	                        # which will later be set by auto_commit
 35168	                        value = getattr(data, key)
 35169	                        if value is not None:
 35170	                            return value
 35171	                        else:
 35172	                            return lambda: getattr(data, key)()
 35173	                    return super().__getattribute__(key)
 35174	
 35175	                def __delattr__(self, key):
 35176	                    if key in ("now", "deferred"):
 35177	                        setattr(data, key, None)
 35178	                    else:
 35179	                        super().__delattr__(self, key)
 35180	
 35181	                @property
 35182	                def dirty(_):
 35183	                    return data.dirty
 35184	
 35185	                @dirty.setter
 35186	                def dirty(_, value):
 35187	                    data.dirty = value
 35188	
 35189	            return Deferred()
 35190	
 35191	        def __set__(self, instance, value):
 35192	            raise ValueError(
 35193	                f"decorated {name} can't be mocked; "
 35194	                f"mock '{name}.now' and/or '{name}.deferred'.")
 35195	
 35196	    return DeferrerProperty()

 35730	## Disabler is a call-back class for check box that can disable/enable other
 35731	## widgets according to state (checked/unchecked, enabled/disable) of the
 35732	## given check box
 35733	##
 35734	## Tricky: if self.propagateState is True (default), then if check box is
 35735	## disabled the related widgets will be disabled (even if the checkbox is
 35736	## checked). If self.propagateState is False, the related widgets will be
 35737	## disabled/enabled if check box is checked/clear, disregarding whether the
 35738	## check box itself is enabled or not. (If you don't understand, see the
 35739	## code :-)
 35740	DISABLER = 1
 35741	HIDER = 2
 35742	
 35743	
 35744	# noinspection PyShadowingBuiltins
 35745	class Disabler:
 35746	    def __init__(self, widget, master, valueName, propagateState=True,
 35747	                 type=DISABLER):
 35748	        self.widget = widget
 35749	        self.master = master
 35750	        self.valueName = valueName
 35751	        self.propagateState = propagateState
 35752	        self.type = type
 35753	
 35754	    def __call__(self, *value):
 35755	        currState = self.widget.isEnabled()
 35756	        if currState or not self.propagateState:
 35757	            if len(value):
 35758	                disabled = not value[0]
 35759	            else:
 35760	                disabled = not getdeepattr(self.master, self.valueName)
 35761	        else:
 35762	            disabled = True
 35763	        for w in self.widget.disables:
 35764	            if isinstance(w, tuple):
 35765	                if isinstance(w[0], int):
 35766	                    i = 1
 35767	                    if w[0] == -1:
 35768	                        disabled = not disabled
 35769	                else:
 35770	                    i = 0
 35771	                if self.type == DISABLER:
 35772	                    w[i].setDisabled(disabled)
 35773	                elif self.type == HIDER:
 35774	                    if disabled:
 35775	                        w[i].hide()
 35776	                    else:
 35777	                        w[i].show()
 35778	                if hasattr(w[i], "makeConsistent"):
 35779	                    w[i].makeConsistent()
 35780	            else:
 35781	                if self.type == DISABLER:
 35782	                    w.setDisabled(disabled)
 35783	                elif self.type == HIDER:
 35784	                    if disabled:
 35785	                        w.hide()
 35786	                    else:
 35787	                        w.show()

 36350	class FloatSlider(Slider):
 36351	    """
 36352	    Slider for continuous values.
 36353	
 36354	    The slider is derived from `QtGui.QSlider`, but maps from its discrete
 36355	    numbers to the desired continuous interval.
 36356	    """
 36357	    valueChangedFloat = Signal(float)
 36358	
 36359	    def __init__(self, orientation, min_value, max_value, step, parent=None):
 36360	        super().__init__(orientation, parent)
 36361	        self.setScale(min_value, max_value, step)
 36362	        self.valueChanged[int].connect(self._send_value)
 36363	
 36364	    def _update(self):
 36365	        self.setSingleStep(1)
 36366	        if self.min_value != self.max_value:
 36367	            self.setEnabled(True)
 36368	            self.setMinimum(int(round(self.min_value / self.step)))
 36369	            self.setMaximum(int(round(self.max_value / self.step)))
 36370	        else:
 36371	            self.setEnabled(False)
 36372	
 36373	    def _send_value(self, slider_value):
 36374	        value = min(max(slider_value * self.step, self.min_value),
 36375	                    self.max_value)
 36376	        self.valueChangedFloat.emit(value)
 36377	
 36378	    def setValue(self, value):
 36379	        """
 36380	        Set current value. The value is divided by `step`
 36381	
 36382	        Args:
 36383	            value: new value
 36384	        """
 36385	        super().setValue(int(round(value / self.step)))

 36388	        """
 36389	        Set slider's ranges (compatibility with qwtSlider).
 36390	
 36391	        Args:
 36392	            minValue (float): minimal value
 36393	            maxValue (float): maximal value
 36394	            step (float): step
 36395	        """
 36396	        if minValue >= maxValue:
 36397	            ## It would be more logical to disable the slider in this case
 36398	            ## (self.setEnabled(False))
 36399	            ## However, we do nothing to keep consistency with Qwt
 36400	            # TODO If it's related to Qwt, remove it
 36401	            return
 36402	        if step <= 0 or step > (maxValue - minValue):
 36403	            if isinstance(maxValue, int) and isinstance(minValue, int):
 36404	                step = 1
 36405	            else:
 36406	                step = float(minValue - maxValue) / 100.0
 36407	        self.min_value = float(minValue)
 36408	        self.max_value = float(maxValue)
 36409	        self.step = step
 36410	        self._update()

 36426	class ControlGetter:
 36427	    """
 36428	    Provide access to GUI elements based on their corresponding attributes
 36429	    in widget.
 36430	
 36431	    Every widget has an attribute `controls` that is an instance of this
 36432	    class, which uses the `controlled_attributes` dictionary to retrieve the
 36433	    control (e.g. `QCheckBox`, `QComboBox`...) corresponding to the attribute.
 36434	    For `OWComponents`, it returns its controls so that subsequent
 36435	    `__getattr__` will retrieve the control.

 36437	    def __init__(self, widget):

 36441	        widget = self.widget
 36442	        callfronts = widget.controlled_attributes.get(name, None)
 36443	        if callfronts is None:
 36444	            # This must be an OWComponent
 36445	            try:
 36446	                return getattr(widget, name).controls
 36447	            except AttributeError:
 36448	                raise AttributeError(
 36449	                    "'{}' is not an attribute related to a gui element or "
 36450	                    "component".format(name))
 36451	        else:

 36865	def _sizeof_fmt(num: float, size_qualifier: str) -> str:
 36866	    """
 36867	    Return size in human readable format.
 36868	
 36869	    Parameters
 36870	    ----------
 36871	    num : int
 36872	        Size in bytes.
 36873	    size_qualifier : str
 36874	        Either empty, or '+' (if lower bound).
 36875	
 36876	    Returns
 36877	    -------
 36878	    str
 36879	        Size in human readable format.
 36880	
 36881	    Examples
 36882	    --------
 36883	    >>> _sizeof_fmt(23028, '')
 36884	    '22.5 KB'
 36885	
 36886	    >>> _sizeof_fmt(23028, '+')
 36887	    '22.5+ KB'
 36888	    """
 36889	    for x in ["bytes", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"]:
 36890	        if num < 1024.0:
 36891	            return f"{num:3.1f}{size_qualifier} {x}"
 36892	        num /= 1024.0

 37707	
 37708	    Parameters
 37709	    ----------
 37710	    formatter : `DataFrameFormatter`
 37711	        Instance of `DataFrameFormatter`.
 37712	    multicolumn: bool, optional
 37713	        Whether to use \multicolumn macro.
 37714	    multicolumn_format: str, optional

 37717	        Whether to use \multirow macro.
 37718	
 37719	    """
 37720	
 37721	    def __init__(
 37722	        self,
 37723	        formatter: DataFrameFormatter,
 37724	        multicolumn: bool = False,
 37725	        multicolumn_format: str | None = None,
 37726	        multirow: bool = False,
 37727	    ) -> None:
 37728	        self.fmt = formatter
 37729	        self.frame = self.fmt.frame
 37730	        self.multicolumn = multicolumn
 37731	        self.multicolumn_format = multicolumn_format
 37732	        self.multirow = multirow
 37733	        self.clinebuf: list[list[int]] = []
 37734	        self.strcols = self._get_strcols()
 37735	        self.strrows = list(zip(*self.strcols))
 37736	
 37737	    def get_strrow(self, row_num: int) -> str:
 37738	        """Get string representation of the row."""
 37739	        row = self.strrows[row_num]
 37740	
 37741	        is_multicol = (
 37742	            row_num < self.column_levels and self.fmt.header and self.multicolumn
 37743	        )
 37744	
 37745	        is_multirow = (
 37746	            row_num >= self.header_levels
 37747	            and self.fmt.index
 37748	            and self.multirow
 37749	            and self.index_levels > 1
 37750	        )
 37751	
 37752	        is_cline_maybe_required = is_multirow and row_num < len(self.strrows) - 1
 37753	
 37754	        crow = self._preprocess_row(row)
 37755	
 37756	        if is_multicol:
 37757	            crow = self._format_multicolumn(crow)
 37758	        if is_multirow:
 37759	            crow = self._format_multirow(crow, row_num)
 37760	
 37761	        lst = []
 37762	        lst.append(" & ".join(crow))
 37763	        lst.append(" \\\\")
 37764	        if is_cline_maybe_required:
 37765	            cline = self._compose_cline(row_num, len(self.strcols))
 37766	            lst.append(cline)

 37792	        if self.fmt.frame.empty:

 37794	        else:

 37796

 37865	                    f"\\multicolumn{{{ncol:d}}}{{{self.multicolumn_format}}}"
 37866	                    f"{{{coltext.strip()}}}"
 37867	                )

 37869	            else:
 37870	                row2.append(coltext)

 37872	        for c in row[self.index_levels :]:
 37873	            # if next col has text, write the previous
 37874	            if c.strip():
 37875	                if coltext:
 37876	                    append_col()
 37877	                coltext = c
 37878	                ncol = 1
 37879	            # if not, add it to the previous multicolumn

 37887	    def _format_multirow(self, row: list[str], i: int) -> list[str]:
 37888	        r"""
 37889	        Check following rows, whether row should be a multirow
 37890	
 37891	        e.g.:     becomes:
 37892	        a & 0 &   \multirow{2}{*}{a} & 0 &
 37893	          & 1 &     & 1 &
 37894	        b & 0 &   \cline{1-2}
 37895	                  b & 0 &
 37896	        """
 37897	        for j in range(self.index_levels):
 37898	            if row[j].strip():
 37899	                nrow = 1
 37900	                for r in self.strrows[i + 1 :]:
 37901	                    if not r[j].strip():
 37902	                        nrow += 1
 37903	                    else:
 37904	                        break
 37905	                if nrow > 1:
 37906	                    # overwrite non-multirow entry
 37907	                    row[j] = f"\\multirow{{{nrow:d}}}{{*}}{{{row[j].strip()}}}"
 37908	                    # save when to end the current block with \cline
 37909	                    self.clinebuf.append([i + nrow - 1, j + 1])
 37910	        return row

 37912	    def _compose_cline(self, i: int, icol: int) -> str:
 37913	        """
 37914	        Create clines after multirow-blocks are finished.
 37915	        """
 37916	        lst = []
 37917	        for cl in self.clinebuf:
 37918	            if cl[0] == i:
 37919	                lst.append(f"\n\\cline{{{cl[1]:d}-{icol:d}}}")
 37920	                # remove entries that have been written to buffer
 37921	                self.clinebuf = [x for x in self.clinebuf if x[0] != i]
 37922	        return "".join(lst)

 38506	def adjoin(space: int, *lists: list[str], **kwargs) -> str:
 38507	    """
 38508	    Glues together two sets of strings using the amount of space requested.
 38509	    The idea is to prettify.
 38510	
 38511	    ----------
 38512	    space : int
 38513	        number of spaces for padding
 38514	    lists : str
 38515	        list of str which being joined
 38516	    strlen : callable
 38517	        function used to calculate the length of each str. Needed for unicode
 38518	        handling.
 38519	    justfunc : callable
 38520	        function used to justify str. Needed for unicode handling.

 38555	#
 38556	# pprinting utility functions for generating Unicode text or

 38558	# Try to use these as much as possible rather than rolling your own.

 38577	def _pprint_seq(
 38578	    seq: Sequence, _nest_lvl: int = 0, max_seq_items: int | None = None, **kwds
 38579	) -> str:
 38580	    """
 38581	    internal. pprinter for iterables. you should probably use pprint_thing()
 38582	    rather than calling this directly.
 38583	
 38584	    bounds length of printed sequence, depending on options
 38585	    """
 38586	    if isinstance(seq, set):
 38587	        fmt = "{{{body}}}"
 38588	    else:
 38589	        fmt = "[{body}]" if hasattr(seq, "__setitem__") else "({body})"
 38590	
 38591	    if max_seq_items is False:
 38592	        nitems = len(seq)
 38593	    else:
 38594	        nitems = max_seq_items or get_option("max_seq_items") or len(seq)
 38595	
 38596	    s = iter(seq)
 38597	    # handle sets, no slicing
 38598	    r = [
 38599	        pprint_thing(next(s), _nest_lvl + 1, max_seq_items=max_seq_items, **kwds)
 38600	        for i in range(min(nitems, len(seq)))
 38601	    ]
 38602	    body = ", ".join(r)
 38603	
 38604	    if nitems < len(seq):
 38605	        body += ", ..."
 38606	    elif isinstance(seq, tuple) and len(seq) == 1:
 38607	        body += ","
 38608	
 38609	    return fmt.format(body=body)

 38617	    rather than calling this directly.

 38633	                val=pprint_thing(v, _nest_lvl + 1, max_seq_items=max_seq_items, **kwds),
 38634	            )
 38635	        )
 38636

 38638	        return fmt.format(things=", ".join(pairs) + ", ...")

 38643	def pprint_thing(
 38644	    thing: Any,
 38645	    _nest_lvl: int = 0,
 38646	    escape_chars: EscapeChars | None = None,
 38647	    default_escapes: bool = False,
 38648	    quote_strings: bool = False,
 38649	    max_seq_items: int | None = None,
 38650	) -> str:
 38651	    """
 38652	    This function is the sanctioned way of converting objects
 38653	    to a string representation and properly handles nested sequences.
 38654	
 38655	    Parameters
 38656	    ----------
 38657	    thing : anything to be formatted
 38658	    _nest_lvl : internal use only. pprint_thing() is mutually-recursive
 38659	        with pprint_sequence, this argument is used to keep track of the
 38660	        current nesting level, and limit it.
 38661	    escape_chars : list or dict, optional
 38662	        Characters to escape. If a dict is passed the values are the
 38663	        replacements
 38664	    default_escapes : bool, default False
 38665	        Whether the input escape characters replaces or adds to the defaults
 38666	    max_seq_items : int or None, default None
 38667	        Pass through to other pretty printers to limit sequence printing
 38668	
 38669	    Returns
 38670	    -------
 38671	    str
 38672	    """
 38673	
 38674	    def as_escaped_string(
 38675	        thing: Any, escape_chars: EscapeChars | None = escape_chars
 38676	    ) -> str:
 38677	        translate = {"\t": r"\t", "\n": r"\n", "\r": r"\r"}
 38678	        if isinstance(escape_chars, dict):
 38679	            if default_escapes:
 38680	                translate.update(escape_chars)
 38681	            else:
 38682	                translate = escape_chars
 38683	            escape_chars = list(escape_chars.keys())
 38684	        else:
 38685	            escape_chars = escape_chars or ()
 38686	
 38687	        result = str(thing)
 38688	        for c in escape_chars:
 38689	            result = result.replace(c, translate[c])
 38690	        return result
 38691	
 38692	    if hasattr(thing, "__next__"):
 38693	        return str(thing)
 38694	    elif isinstance(thing, dict) and _nest_lvl < get_option(
 38695	        "display.pprint_nest_depth"
 38696	    ):
 38697	        result = _pprint_dict(
 38698	            thing, _nest_lvl, quote_strings=True, max_seq_items=max_seq_items
 38699	        )
 38700	    elif is_sequence(thing) and _nest_lvl < get_option("display.pprint_nest_depth"):
 38701	        result = _pprint_seq(
 38702	            thing,
 38703	            _nest_lvl,
 38704	            escape_chars=escape_chars,
 38705	            quote_strings=quote_strings,
 38706	            max_seq_items=max_seq_items,
 38707	        )
 38708	    elif isinstance(thing, str) and quote_strings:
 38709	        result = f"'{as_escaped_string(thing)}'"
 38710	    else:
 38711	        result = as_escaped_string(thing)
 38712	
 38713	    return result

 38766	def format_object_summary(
 38767	    obj,
 38768	    formatter: Callable,
 38769	    is_justify: bool = True,
 38770	    name: str | None = None,
 38771	    indent_for_name: bool = True,
 38772	    line_break_each_value: bool = False,
 38773	) -> str:
 38774	    """
 38775	    Return the formatted obj as a unicode string
 38776	
 38777	    Parameters
 38778	    ----------
 38779	    obj : object
 38780	        must be iterable and support __getitem__
 38781	    formatter : callable
 38782	        string formatter for an element
 38783	    is_justify : bool
 38784	        should justify the display
 38785	    name : name, optional
 38786	        defaults to the class name of the obj
 38787	    indent_for_name : bool, default True
 38788	        Whether subsequent lines should be indented to
 38789	        align with the name.
 38790	    line_break_each_value : bool, default False
 38791	        If True, inserts a line break for each value of ``obj``.
 38792	        If False, only break lines when the a line of values gets wider
 38793	        than the display width.
 38794	
 38795	    Returns
 38796	    -------
 38797	    summary string
 38798	    """
 38799	    from pandas.io.formats.console import get_console_size
 38800	    from pandas.io.formats.format import get_adjustment
 38801	
 38802	    display_width, _ = get_console_size()
 38803	    if display_width is None:
 38804	        display_width = get_option("display.width") or 80
 38805	    if name is None:
 38806	        name = type(obj).__name__
 38807	
 38808	    if indent_for_name:
 38809	        name_len = len(name)
 38810	        space1 = f'\n{(" " * (name_len + 1))}'
 38811	        space2 = f'\n{(" " * (name_len + 2))}'
 38812	    else:
 38813	        space1 = "\n"
 38814	        space2 = "\n "  # space for the opening '['
 38815	
 38816	    n = len(obj)
 38817	    if line_break_each_value:
 38818	        # If we want to vertically align on each value of obj, we need to
 38819	        # separate values by a line break and indent the values
 38820	        sep = ",\n " + " " * len(name)
 38821	    else:
 38822	        sep = ","
 38823	    max_seq_items = get_option("display.max_seq_items") or n
 38824	
 38825	    # are we a truncated display
 38826	    is_truncated = n > max_seq_items
 38827	
 38828	    # adj can optionally handle unicode eastern asian width
 38829	    adj = get_adjustment()
 38830	
 38831	    def _extend_line(
 38832	        s: str, line: str, value: str, display_width: int, next_line_prefix: str
 38833	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
 38834	        if adj.len(line.rstrip()) + adj.len(value.rstrip()) >= display_width:
 38835	            s += line.rstrip()
 38836	            line = next_line_prefix
 38837	        line += value
 38838	        return s, line
 38839	
 38840	    def best_len(values: list[str]) -> int:
 38841	        if values:
 38842	            return max(adj.len(x) for x in values)
 38843	        else:
 38844	            return 0
 38845	
 38846	    close = ", "
 38847	
 38848	    if n == 0:
 38849	        summary = f"[]{close}"
 38850	    elif n == 1 and not line_break_each_value:
 38851	        first = formatter(obj[0])
 38852	        summary = f"[{first}]{close}"
 38853	    elif n == 2 and not line_break_each_value:
 38854	        first = formatter(obj[0])
 38855	        last = formatter(obj[-1])
 38856	        summary = f"[{first}, {last}]{close}"
 38857	    else:
 38858	        if max_seq_items == 1:
 38859	            # If max_seq_items=1 show only last element
 38860	            head = []
 38861	            tail = [formatter(x) for x in obj[-1:]]
 38862	        elif n > max_seq_items:
 38863	            n = min(max_seq_items // 2, 10)
 38864	            head = [formatter(x) for x in obj[:n]]
 38865	            tail = [formatter(x) for x in obj[-n:]]
 38866	        else:
 38867	            head = []
 38868	            tail = [formatter(x) for x in obj]
 38869	
 38870	        # adjust all values to max length if needed
 38871	        if is_justify:
 38872	            if line_break_each_value:
 38873	                # Justify each string in the values of head and tail, so the
 38874	                # strings will right align when head and tail are stacked
 38875	                # vertically.
 38876	                head, tail = _justify(head, tail)
 38877	            elif is_truncated or not (
 38878	                len(", ".join(head)) < display_width
 38879	                and len(", ".join(tail)) < display_width
 38880	            ):
 38881	                # Each string in head and tail should align with each other
 38882	                max_length = max(best_len(head), best_len(tail))
 38883	                head = [x.rjust(max_length) for x in head]
 38884	                tail = [x.rjust(max_length) for x in tail]
 38885	            # If we are not truncated and we are only a single
 38886	            # line, then don't justify
 38887	
 38888	        if line_break_each_value:
 38889	            # Now head and tail are of type List[Tuple[str]]. Below we
 38890	            # convert them into List[str], so there will be one string per
 38891	            # value. Also truncate items horizontally if wider than
 38892	            # max_space
 38893	            max_space = display_width - len(space2)
 38894	            value = tail[0]
 38895	            for max_items in reversed(range(1, len(value) + 1)):
 38896	                pprinted_seq = _pprint_seq(value, max_seq_items=max_items)
 38897	                if len(pprinted_seq) < max_space:
 38898	                    head = [_pprint_seq(x, max_seq_items=max_items) for x in head]
 38899	                    tail = [_pprint_seq(x, max_seq_items=max_items) for x in tail]
 38900	                    break
 38901	
 38902	        summary = ""
 38903	        line = space2
 38904	
 38905	        for head_value in head:
 38906	            word = head_value + sep + " "
 38907	            summary, line = _extend_line(summary, line, word, display_width, space2)
 38908	
 38909	        if is_truncated:
 38910	            # remove trailing space of last line
 38911	            summary += line.rstrip() + space2 + "..."
 38912	            line = space2
 38913	
 38914	        for tail_item in tail[:-1]:
 38915	            word = tail_item + sep + " "
 38916	            summary, line = _extend_line(summary, line, word, display_width, space2)
 38917	
 38918	        # last value: no sep added + 1 space of width used for trailing ','
 38919	        summary, line = _extend_line(summary, line, tail[-1], display_width - 2, space2)
 38920	        summary += line
 38921	
 38922	        # right now close is either '' or ', '
 38923	        # Now we want to include the ']', but not the maybe space.
 38924	        close = "]" + close.rstrip(" ")
 38925	        summary += close
 38926	
 38927	        if len(summary) > (display_width) or line_break_each_value:
 38928	            summary += space1
 38929	        else:  # one row
 38930	            summary += " "
 38931	
 38932	        # remove initial space
 38933	        summary = "[" + summary[len(space2) :]
 38934	
 38935	    return summary

 38938	def _justify(
 38939	    head: list[Sequence[str]], tail: list[Sequence[str]]
 38940	) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, ...]], list[tuple[str, ...]]]:
 38941	    """
 38942	    Justify items in head and tail, so they are right-aligned when stacked.
 38943	
 38944	    Parameters
 38945	    ----------
 38946	    head : list-like of list-likes of strings
 38947	    tail : list-like of list-likes of strings
 38948	
 38949	    Returns
 38950	    -------
 38951	    tuple of list of tuples of strings
 38952	        Same as head and tail, but items are right aligned when stacked
 38953	        vertically.
 38954	
 38955	    Examples
 38956	    --------
 38957	    >>> _justify([['a', 'b']], [['abc', 'abcd']])
 38958	    ([('  a', '   b')], [('abc', 'abcd')])
 38959	    """
 38960	    combined = head + tail
 38961	
 38962	    # For each position for the sequences in ``combined``,
 38963	    # find the length of the largest string.
 38964	    max_length = [0] * len(combined[0])
 38965	    for inner_seq in combined:
 38966	        length = [len(item) for item in inner_seq]
 38967	        max_length = [max(x, y) for x, y in zip(max_length, length)]
 38968	
 38969	    # justify each item in each list-like in head and tail using max_length
 38970	    head_tuples = [
 38971	        tuple(x.rjust(max_len) for x, max_len in zip(seq, max_length)) for seq in head
 38972	    ]
 38973	    tail_tuples = [
 38974	        tuple(x.rjust(max_len) for x, max_len in zip(seq, max_length)) for seq in tail
 38975	    ]
 38976	    return head_tuples, tail_tuples

 39448	def _is_metadata_of(group: Node, parent_group: Node) -> bool:
 39449	    """Check if a given group is a metadata group for a given parent_group."""
 39450	    if group._v_depth <= parent_group._v_depth:
 39451	        return False
 39452	
 39453	    current = group
 39454	    while current._v_depth > 1:
 39455	        parent = current._v_parent
 39456	        if parent == parent_group and current._v_name == "meta":
 39457	            return True
 39458	        current = current._v_parent
 39459	    return False

 40791	    def _create_nodes_and_group(self, key: str) -> Node:

 40816	
 40817	    Parameters
 40818	    ----------
 40819	    store : HDFStore

 40822	    where : the where of the query

 40825	    stop  : the passed stop value (default is None)

 40828	    chunksize : the passed chunking value (default is 100000)
 40829	    auto_close : bool, default False
 40830	        Whether to automatically close the store at the end of iteration.
 40831	    """
 40832	
 40833	    chunksize: int | None
 40834	    store: HDFStore

 40836	
 40837	    def __init__(
 40838	        self,
 40839	        store: HDFStore,
 40840	        s: GenericFixed | Table,
 40841	        func,
 40842	        where,
 40843	        nrows,
 40844	        start=None,
 40845	        stop=None,
 40846	        iterator: bool = False,
 40847	        chunksize: int | None = None,
 40848	        auto_close: bool = False,
 40849	    ) -> None:
 40850	        self.store = store
 40851	        self.s = s
 40852	        self.func = func
 40853	        self.where = where
 40854	
 40855	        # set start/stop if they are not set if we are a table
 40856	        if self.s.is_table:
 40857	            if nrows is None:
 40858	                nrows = 0
 40859	            if start is None:
 40860	                start = 0
 40861	            if stop is None:
 40862	                stop = nrows
 40863	            stop = min(nrows, stop)
 40864	
 40865	        self.nrows = nrows
 40866	        self.start = start
 40867	        self.stop = stop
 40868	
 40869	        self.coordinates = None
 40870	        if iterator or chunksize is not None:
 40871	            if chunksize is None:
 40872	                chunksize = 100000
 40873	            self.chunksize = int(chunksize)
 40874	        else:
 40875	            self.chunksize = None
 40876	
 40877	        self.auto_close = auto_close
 40878	
 40879	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator:
 40880	        # iterate
 40881	        current = self.start
 40882	        if self.coordinates is None:
 40883	            raise ValueError("Cannot iterate until get_result is called.")
 40884	        while current < self.stop:
 40885	            stop = min(current + self.chunksize, self.stop)
 40886	            value = self.func(None, None, self.coordinates[current:stop])
 40887	            current = stop
 40888	            if value is None or not len(value):
 40889	                continue
 40890	
 40891	            yield value
 40892	
 40893	        self.close()
 40894

 40897	            self.store.close()
 40898	
 40899	    def get_result(self, coordinates: bool = False):
 40900	        #  return the actual iterator
 40901	        if self.chunksize is not None:
 40902	            if not isinstance(self.s, Table):
 40903	                raise TypeError("can only use an iterator or chunksize on a table")
 40904	
 40905	            self.coordinates = self.s.read_coordinates(where=self.where)
 40906	
 40907	            return self
 40908	
 40909	        # if specified read via coordinates (necessary for multiple selections
 40910	        if coordinates:
 40911	            if not isinstance(self.s, Table):
 40912	                raise TypeError("can only read_coordinates on a table")
 40913	            where = self.s.read_coordinates(
 40914	                where=self.where, start=self.start, stop=self.stop
 40915	            )
 40916	        else:
 40917	            where = self.where
 40918	
 40919	        # directly return the result
 40920	        results = self.func(self.start, self.stop, where)
 40921	        self.close()

 41422	    def convert(self, values: np.ndarray, nan_rep, encoding: str, errors: str):
 41423	        """
 41424	        Convert the data from this selection to the appropriate pandas type.
 41425	
 41426	        Parameters
 41427	        ----------
 41428	        values : np.ndarray
 41429	        nan_rep :
 41430	        encoding : str
 41431	        errors : str
 41432	
 41433	        Returns
 41434	        -------
 41435	        index : listlike to become an Index
 41436	        data : ndarraylike to become a column
 41437	        """
 41438	        assert isinstance(values, np.ndarray), type(values)
 41439	
 41440	        # values is a recarray
 41441	        if values.dtype.fields is not None:
 41442	            values = values[self.cname]
 41443	
 41444	        assert self.typ is not None
 41445	        if self.dtype is None:
 41446	            # Note: in tests we never have timedelta64 or datetime64,
 41447	            #  so the _get_data_and_dtype_name may be unnecessary
 41448	            converted, dtype_name = _get_data_and_dtype_name(values)
 41449	            kind = _dtype_to_kind(dtype_name)
 41450	        else:
 41451	            converted = values
 41452	            dtype_name = self.dtype
 41453	            kind = self.kind
 41454	
 41455	        assert isinstance(converted, np.ndarray)  # for mypy
 41456	
 41457	        # use the meta if needed
 41458	        meta = _ensure_decoded(self.meta)
 41459	        metadata = self.metadata
 41460	        ordered = self.ordered
 41461	        tz = self.tz
 41462	
 41463	        assert dtype_name is not None
 41464	        # convert to the correct dtype
 41465	        dtype = _ensure_decoded(dtype_name)
 41466	
 41467	        # reverse converts
 41468	        if dtype == "datetime64":
 41469	            # recreate with tz if indicated
 41470	            converted = _set_tz(converted, tz, coerce=True)
 41471	
 41472	        elif dtype == "timedelta64":
 41473	            converted = np.asarray(converted, dtype="m8[ns]")
 41474	        elif dtype == "date":
 41475	            try:
 41476	                converted = np.asarray(
 41477	                    [date.fromordinal(v) for v in converted], dtype=object
 41478	                )
 41479	            except ValueError:
 41480	                converted = np.asarray(
 41481	                    [date.fromtimestamp(v) for v in converted], dtype=object
 41482	                )
 41483	
 41484	        elif meta == "category":
 41485	            # we have a categorical
 41486	            categories = metadata
 41487	            codes = converted.ravel()
 41488	
 41489	            # if we have stored a NaN in the categories
 41490	            # then strip it; in theory we could have BOTH
 41491	            # -1s in the codes and nulls :<
 41492	            if categories is None:
 41493	                # Handle case of NaN-only categorical columns in which case
 41494	                # the categories are an empty array; when this is stored,
 41495	                # pytables cannot write a zero-len array, so on readback
 41496	                # the categories would be None and `read_hdf()` would fail.
 41497	                categories = Index([], dtype=np.float64)
 41498	            else:
 41499	                mask = isna(categories)
 41500	                if mask.any():
 41501	                    categories = categories[~mask]
 41502	                    codes[codes != -1] -= mask.astype(int).cumsum()._values
 41503	
 41504	            converted = Categorical.from_codes(
 41505	                codes, categories=categories, ordered=ordered
 41506	            )
 41507	
 41508	        else:
 41509	            try:
 41510	                converted = converted.astype(dtype, copy=False)
 41511	            except TypeError:
 41512	                converted = converted.astype("O", copy=False)
 41513	
 41514	        # convert nans / decode
 41515	        if _ensure_decoded(kind) == "string":
 41516	            converted = _unconvert_string_array(
 41517	                converted, nan_rep=nan_rep, encoding=encoding, errors=errors
 41518	            )
 41519	
 41520	        return self.values, converted

 42592	    def create_index(
 42593	        self, columns=None, optlevel=None, kind: str | None = None
 42594	    ) -> None:
 42595	        """
 42596	        Create a pytables index on the specified columns.
 42597	
 42598	        Parameters
 42599	        ----------
 42600	        columns : None, bool, or listlike[str]
 42601	            Indicate which columns to create an index on.
 42602	
 42603	            * False : Do not create any indexes.
 42604	            * True : Create indexes on all columns.
 42605	            * None : Create indexes on all columns.
 42606	            * listlike : Create indexes on the given columns.
 42607	
 42608	        optlevel : int or None, default None
 42609	            Optimization level, if None, pytables defaults to 6.
 42610	        kind : str or None, default None
 42611	            Kind of index, if None, pytables defaults to "medium".
 42612	
 42613	        Raises
 42614	        ------
 42615	        TypeError if trying to create an index on a complex-type column.
 42616	
 42617	        Notes
 42618	        -----
 42619	        Cannot index Time64Col or ComplexCol.
 42620	        Pytables must be >= 3.0.
 42621	        """
 42622	        if not self.infer_axes():
 42623	            return
 42624	        if columns is False:
 42625	            return
 42626	
 42627	        # index all indexables and data_columns
 42628	        if columns is None or columns is True:
 42629	            columns = [a.cname for a in self.axes if a.is_data_indexable]
 42630	        if not isinstance(columns, (tuple, list)):
 42631	            columns = [columns]
 42632	
 42633	        kw = {}
 42634	        if optlevel is not None:
 42635	            kw["optlevel"] = optlevel
 42636	        if kind is not None:
 42637	            kw["kind"] = kind
 42638	
 42639	        table = self.table
 42640	        for c in columns:
 42641	            v = getattr(table.cols, c, None)
 42642	            if v is not None:
 42643	                # remove the index if the kind/optlevel have changed
 42644	                if v.is_indexed:
 42645	                    index = v.index
 42646	                    cur_optlevel = index.optlevel
 42647	                    cur_kind = index.kind
 42648	
 42649	                    if kind is not None and cur_kind != kind:
 42650	                        v.remove_index()
 42651	                    else:
 42652	                        kw["kind"] = cur_kind
 42653	
 42654	                    if optlevel is not None and cur_optlevel != optlevel:
 42655	                        v.remove_index()
 42656	                    else:
 42657	                        kw["optlevel"] = cur_optlevel
 42658	
 42659	                # create the index
 42660	                if not v.is_indexed:
 42661	                    if v.type.startswith("complex"):
 42662	                        raise TypeError(
 42663	                            "Columns containing complex values can be stored but "
 42664	                            "cannot be indexed when using table format. Either use "
 42665	                            "fixed format, set index=False, or do not include "
 42666	                            "the columns containing complex values to "
 42667	                            "data_columns when initializing the table."
 42668	                        )
 42669	                    v.create_index(**kw)
 42670	            elif c in self.non_index_axes[0][1]:

 42672	                raise AttributeError(

 42717	    def validate_data_columns(self, data_columns, min_itemsize, non_index_axes):
 42718	        """
 42719	        take the input data_columns and min_itemize and create a data
 42720	        columns spec
 42721	        """
 42722	        if not len(non_index_axes):
 42723	            return []
 42724	
 42725	        axis, axis_labels = non_index_axes[0]
 42726	        info = self.info.get(axis, {})
 42727	        if info.get("type") == "MultiIndex" and data_columns:
 42728	            raise ValueError(
 42729	                f"cannot use a multi-index on axis [{axis}] with "
 42730	                f"data_columns {data_columns}"
 42731	            )
 42732	
 42733	        # evaluate the passed data_columns, True == use all columns
 42734	        # take only valid axis labels
 42735	        if data_columns is True:
 42736	            data_columns = list(axis_labels)
 42737	        elif data_columns is None:
 42738	            data_columns = []
 42739	
 42740	        # if min_itemsize is a dict, add the keys (exclude 'values')
 42741	        if isinstance(min_itemsize, dict):
 42742	            existing_data_columns = set(data_columns)
 42743	            data_columns = list(data_columns)  # ensure we do not modify
 42744	            data_columns.extend(
 42745	                [
 42746	                    k
 42747	                    for k in min_itemsize.keys()
 42748	                    if k != "values" and k not in existing_data_columns
 42749	                ]
 42750	            )
 42751	
 42752	        # return valid columns in the order of our axis

 43306	    def write_data(self, chunksize: int | None, dropna: bool = False) -> None:

 43311	        nrows = self.nrows_expected

 43314	        masks = []

 43318	                # column, otherwise ignore the mask
 43319	                mask = isna(a.data).all(axis=0)
 43320	                if isinstance(mask, np.ndarray):
 43321	                    masks.append(mask.astype("u1", copy=False))
 43322	
 43323	        # consolidate masks
 43324	        if len(masks):
 43325	            mask = masks[0]
 43326	            for m in masks[1:]:
 43327	                mask = mask & m
 43328	            mask = mask.ravel()
 43329	        else:
 43330	            mask = None
 43331	
 43332	        # broadcast the indexes if needed
 43333	        indexes = [a.cvalues for a in self.index_axes]
 43334	        nindexes = len(indexes)
 43335	        assert nindexes == 1, nindexes  # ensures we dont need to broadcast
 43336

 43365	    def write_data_chunk(
 43366	        self,
 43367	        rows: np.ndarray,
 43368	        indexes: list[np.ndarray],
 43369	        mask: npt.NDArray[np.bool_] | None,
 43370	        values: list[np.ndarray],
 43371	    ) -> None:
 43372	        """
 43373	        Parameters
 43374	        ----------
 43375	        rows : an empty memory space where we are putting the chunk
 43376	        indexes : an array of the indexes
 43377	        mask : an array of the masks
 43378	        values : an array of the values
 43379	        """
 43380	        # 0 len
 43381	        for v in values:
 43382	            if not np.prod(v.shape):
 43383	                return
 43384	
 43385	        nrows = indexes[0].shape[0]
 43386	        if nrows != len(rows):
 43387	            rows = np.empty(nrows, dtype=self.dtype)
 43388	        names = self.dtype.names
 43389	        nindexes = len(indexes)
 43390	
 43391	        # indexes
 43392	        for i, idx in enumerate(indexes):
 43393	            rows[names[i]] = idx
 43394	
 43395	        # values
 43396	        for i, v in enumerate(values):
 43397	            rows[names[i + nindexes]] = v
 43398	
 43399	        # mask
 43400	        if mask is not None:
 43401	            m = ~mask.ravel().astype(bool, copy=False)
 43402	            if not m.all():
 43403	                rows = rows[m]
 43404	
 43405	        if len(rows):
 43406	            self.table.append(rows)
 43407	            self.table.flush()

 43409	    def delete(self, where=None, start: int | None = None, stop: int | None = None):
 43410	        # delete all rows (and return the nrows)
 43411	        if where is None or not len(where):
 43412	            if start is None and stop is None:
 43413	                nrows = self.nrows
 43414	                self._handle.remove_node(self.group, recursive=True)
 43415	            else:
 43416	                # pytables<3.0 would remove a single row with stop=None
 43417	                if stop is None:
 43418	                    stop = self.nrows
 43419	                nrows = self.table.remove_rows(start=start, stop=stop)
 43420	                self.table.flush()
 43421	            return nrows
 43422	
 43423	        # infer the data kind
 43424	        if not self.infer_axes():
 43425	            return None
 43426	
 43427	        # create the selection
 43428	        table = self.table
 43429	        selection = Selection(self, where, start=start, stop=stop)
 43430	        values = selection.select_coords()
 43431	
 43432	        # delete the rows in reverse order
 43433	        sorted_series = Series(values, copy=False).sort_values()
 43434	        ln = len(sorted_series)
 43435	
 43436	        if ln:
 43437	            # construct groups of consecutive rows
 43438	            diff = sorted_series.diff()
 43439	            groups = list(diff[diff > 1].index)
 43440	
 43441	            # 1 group
 43442	            if not len(groups):
 43443	                groups = [0]
 43444	
 43445	            # final element
 43446	            if groups[-1] != ln:
 43447	                groups.append(ln)
 43448	
 43449	            # initial element
 43450	            if groups[0] != 0:
 43451	                groups.insert(0, 0)
 43452	
 43453	            # we must remove in reverse order!
 43454	            pg = groups.pop()
 43455	            for g in reversed(groups):
 43456	                rows = sorted_series.take(range(g, pg))
 43457	                table.remove_rows(
 43458	                    start=rows[rows.index[0]], stop=rows[rows.index[-1]] + 1
 43459	                )
 43460	                pg = g
 43461	
 43462	            self.table.flush()
 43463	
 43464	        # return the number of rows removed
 43465	        return ln

 44282	class TablePlotter:
 44283	    """
 44284	    Layout some DataFrames in vertical/horizontal layout for explanation.
 44285	    Used in merging.rst
 44286	    """
 44287	
 44288	    def __init__(
 44289	        self,
 44290	        cell_width: float = 0.37,
 44291	        cell_height: float = 0.25,
 44292	        font_size: float = 7.5,
 44293	    ) -> None:
 44294	        self.cell_width = cell_width
 44295	        self.cell_height = cell_height
 44296	        self.font_size = font_size
 44297	
 44298	    def _shape(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[int, int]:
 44299	        """
 44300	        Calculate table shape considering index levels.
 44301	        """
 44302	        row, col = df.shape
 44303	        return row + df.columns.nlevels, col + df.index.nlevels
 44304	
 44305	    def _get_cells(self, left, right, vertical) -> tuple[int, int]:
 44306	        """
 44307	        Calculate appropriate figure size based on left and right data.
 44308	        """
 44309	        if vertical:
 44310	            # calculate required number of cells
 44311	            vcells = max(sum(self._shape(df)[0] for df in left), self._shape(right)[0])
 44312	            hcells = max(self._shape(df)[1] for df in left) + self._shape(right)[1]
 44313	        else:
 44314	            vcells = max([self._shape(df)[0] for df in left] + [self._shape(right)[0]])
 44315	            hcells = sum([self._shape(df)[1] for df in left] + [self._shape(right)[1]])
 44316	        return hcells, vcells
 44317	
 44318	    def plot(self, left, right, labels: Iterable[str] = (), vertical: bool = True):
 44319	        """
 44320	        Plot left / right DataFrames in specified layout.
 44321	
 44322	        Parameters
 44323	        ----------
 44324	        left : list of DataFrames before operation is applied
 44325	        right : DataFrame of operation result
 44326	        labels : list of str to be drawn as titles of left DataFrames
 44327	        vertical : bool, default True
 44328	            If True, use vertical layout. If False, use horizontal layout.
 44329	        """
 44330	        from matplotlib import gridspec
 44331	        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 44332	
 44333	        if not isinstance(left, list):
 44334	            left = [left]
 44335	        left = [self._conv(df) for df in left]
 44336	        right = self._conv(right)
 44337	
 44338	        hcells, vcells = self._get_cells(left, right, vertical)
 44339	
 44340	        if vertical:
 44341	            figsize = self.cell_width * hcells, self.cell_height * vcells
 44342	        else:
 44343	            # include margin for titles
 44344	            figsize = self.cell_width * hcells, self.cell_height * vcells
 44345	        fig = plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
 44346	
 44347	        if vertical:
 44348	            gs = gridspec.GridSpec(len(left), hcells)
 44349	            # left
 44350	            max_left_cols = max(self._shape(df)[1] for df in left)
 44351	            max_left_rows = max(self._shape(df)[0] for df in left)
 44352	            for i, (_left, _label) in enumerate(zip(left, labels)):
 44353	                ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 0:max_left_cols])
 44354	                self._make_table(ax, _left, title=_label, height=1.0 / max_left_rows)
 44355	            # right
 44356	            ax = plt.subplot(gs[:, max_left_cols:])
 44357	            self._make_table(ax, right, title="Result", height=1.05 / vcells)
 44358	            fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.9, bottom=0.05, left=0.05, right=0.95)
 44359	        else:
 44360	            max_rows = max(self._shape(df)[0] for df in left + [right])
 44361	            height = 1.0 / np.max(max_rows)
 44362	            gs = gridspec.GridSpec(1, hcells)
 44363	            # left
 44364	            i = 0
 44365	            for df, _label in zip(left, labels):
 44366	                sp = self._shape(df)
 44367	                ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, i : i + sp[1]])
 44368	                self._make_table(ax, df, title=_label, height=height)
 44369	                i += sp[1]
 44370	            # right
 44371	            ax = plt.subplot(gs[0, i:])
 44372	            self._make_table(ax, right, title="Result", height=height)
 44373	            fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.85, bottom=0.05, left=0.05, right=0.95)
 44374	
 44375	        return fig

 44377	    def _conv(self, data):
 44378	        """
 44379	        Convert each input to appropriate for table outplot.
 44380	        """
 44381	        if isinstance(data, pd.Series):
 44382	            if data.name is None:
 44383	                data = data.to_frame(name="")
 44384	            else:
 44385	                data = data.to_frame()
 44386	        data = data.fillna("NaN")
 44387	        return data

 44389	    def _insert_index(self, data):
 44390	        # insert is destructive
 44391	        data = data.copy()
 44392	        idx_nlevels = data.index.nlevels
 44393	        if idx_nlevels == 1:
 44394	            data.insert(0, "Index", data.index)
 44395	        else:
 44396	            for i in range(idx_nlevels):
 44397	                data.insert(i, f"Index{i}", data.index._get_level_values(i))
 44398	
 44399	        col_nlevels = data.columns.nlevels
 44400	        if col_nlevels > 1:
 44401	            col = data.columns._get_level_values(0)
 44402	            values = [
 44403	                data.columns._get_level_values(i)._values for i in range(1, col_nlevels)
 44404	            ]
 44405	            col_df = pd.DataFrame(values)
 44406	            data.columns = col_df.columns
 44407	            data = pd.concat([col_df, data])
 44408	            data.columns = col
 44409	        return data

 44411	    def _make_table(self, ax, df, title: str, height: float | None = None) -> None:
 44412	        if df is None:
 44413	            ax.set_visible(False)
 44414	            return
 44415	
 44416	        from pandas import plotting
 44417	
 44418	        idx_nlevels = df.index.nlevels
 44419	        col_nlevels = df.columns.nlevels
 44420	        # must be convert here to get index levels for colorization
 44421	        df = self._insert_index(df)
 44422	        tb = plotting.table(ax, df, loc=9)
 44423	        tb.set_fontsize(self.font_size)
 44424	
 44425	        if height is None:
 44426	            height = 1.0 / (len(df) + 1)
 44427	
 44428	        props = tb.properties()
 44429	        for (r, c), cell in props["celld"].items():
 44430	            if c == -1:
 44431	                cell.set_visible(False)
 44432	            elif r < col_nlevels and c < idx_nlevels:
 44433	                cell.set_visible(False)
 44434	            elif r < col_nlevels or c < idx_nlevels:
 44435	                cell.set_facecolor("#AAAAAA")
 44436	            cell.set_height(height)
 44437	
 44438	        ax.set_title(title, size=self.font_size)
 44439	        ax.axis("off")

 44790	        self, console: "Console", options: "ConsoleOptions"
 44791	    ) -> Measurement:
 44792	        max_width = options.max_width
 44793	        if self.width is not None:

 44799	        max_width = sum(
 44800	            self._calculate_column_widths(
 44801	                console, options.update_width(max_width - extra_width)
 44802	            )

 44807	            _measure_column(console, options.update_width(max_width), column)
 44808	            for column in self.columns

 44811	            sum(measurement.minimum for measurement in measurements) + extra_width
 44812	        )

 44814	            sum(measurement.maximum for measurement in measurements) + extra_width
 44815	            if (self.width is None)
